Almost every freaking HIIT workout you have is just glorified cardio with out nearly enough of a break. The workout I did this morning was boasting about how it was reducing the rest time as the workout went on, this is the exact opposite of the philosophy of a HIIT workout guys, stop being stupid just to hit your targeted workout time.

2. Your strength workouts are freaking obsessed with hinges. You need to calm the heck down. I get that you probably have more women using this app than men, but you’re obsessed with this butt building stuff. Swap it up. Get the biceps involved more often.

3. The lack of fast-forward and rewind is absolutely inexcusable for a tech company that owns all their own workout videos.

title: Absolute Beginners
body:
Opted to use the free trial of Apple Fitness. It’s designed for beginners. The lack of overall edibility is alarming. While I found the meditation app to be useful, the inability to actually track your gains, edit the use of free weights or total body weight workout surprising from a technical standpoint. 
To further frustrate me, whilst managing overlapping subscriptions, the icon displayed was Apple Music yet once cancelled it was actually Apple Fitness. I panicked, as I was using this app faithfully for the past first five days of the three month trial. However, I called Apple support with this foolish notion that the free trial would be reinstated. After a 20 minute phone call, I was surprised that Apple stated that there wasn’t anything they could do; thusly, choosing to lose out on a potential subscriber (despite its foibles) as opposed to reinstating the three month trial. 
In short, find an alternative fitness app that will actually track your gains and provide the ability to edit your workout.

title: Amazing if you already know how to exercise safely
body:
I love this app. The trainers are wonderful, and I really enjoy being able to do a variety of activities without having to book a ton of classes. I don’t have a reliable schedule, so it’s a huge relief to be able to do my workouts from home at any point during a 24 hour period. For me, the balance of motivational coaching and comfort and privacy is perfect.

I’ve had a lot of training in a wide variety of physical activities under direct supervision from teachers and coaches. I already know how to do most of the exercises with good and safe technique, and how to create and modify workout plans for myself. From talking to other people, I get the sense that the app may not be as helpful if you’re starting with less experience. As much as I prefer not having to go to the gym, there’s a lot of benefit to learning the fundamentals in person from someone who can give you direct feedback.

The one change I’d personally really like to see is some recognition that exercising relentlessly no matter what is not actually good for your health. It’s kinda disheartening to see something like proper care for an injury or abstaining from overtraining counted as failing at your fitness goal when it’s a vital part of fitness. Some days you should absolutely not be trying to close any rings. It would be great to see a healthier approach to fitness reflected in the app.

title: Why???
body:
Why is this app so obnoxious! Why are the trainers so annoying? There are a few that are great but the majority don’t seem to understand that not every second needs to be filled with their voice and annoying motivational cues. Just instruct, say something when the position or exercise changes. Personality does not need to be forced on us. 

Why is it so difficult to make a custom workout routine???  It’s like playing workout Roulette. Why can I not just simply design the workout I want without having to delete the auto generated ones one workout at a time? As it is all I can do is hope that the algorithm picks what I want or start all over again until it does. The edit functions like everything else Apple these days is half baked. Sure I can remove a workout and add another but can I arrange the order! No of course not. Can I edit the time of a workout that was added? No of course not. WHY OH WHY can I not edit a plan after creating it!!! Why must I delete the entire plan that I took time to build because I would like to add an additional day or decided that I don’t like a particular trainer or music selection. There is no good reason for this it’s just more Apple mediocrity for no real reason. 

It does not need to be this hard guys.

title: Quick Start Ruins It
body:
This Quick Start button is ruining my workouts.

Countless times I’ve switched between workouts and forgotten to hit the Quick Start button. The result? A workout that doesn’t get tracked properly because of an extra step that never used to exist.

You can’t introduce a mandatory step years after people have built habits around using the app and expect there to be no friction. If users want Quick Start, make it optional. For everyone else, please let us disable it or remove it entirely.

This change has made the workout experience worse, not better.

title: Helpful but not perfect
body:
I appreciate the variety of workouts and how the filters work. It’s helpful to build my own plan to keep me accountable, yet customizable for any specific season of my year and work calendar. Streak challenges are motivating because that’s just how my brain works. It might not be for everyone but then, no app is for everyone.

What I wish could change:
• More flexibility in custom plans. Sometimes I want to change the order of that week’s workouts, but I can’t. Or change the type of workout (not just the length) for a specific day but, again, I can’t. 
• Why do German subtitles keep popping up? I don’t see a default for that, and my dubbing language is English. This only started happening in the last couple of months and it’s really annoying. I don’t want to keep stopping to change the CC settings for that video.

title: Not enough flexibility
body:

The autodetect features for workouts leave a lot to be desired. I’m surprised the app can’t recognize sooner when I’ve stopped walking and gotten on a train, bus, or bike — and then remove that period of time that obviously wasn’t part of the walk so it doesn’t get calculated into my health data. 

If I want to correct it, I have to delete the workout and manually log a workout with a more accurate timeframe — or get in the habit of manually logging my workouts start, pause and stop times, on my watch in realtime.

title: They finally added weight training! Still underwhelming overall though.
body:
Apple finally decided to add exercise categories for weight lifting and resistance training! Glad to see them finally add an extremely common workout to the already vast categories that include other wildly popular and commonly practiced workouts like badminton, fencing, and windsurfing! Christ, sometimes I swear Apple intentionally identifies something that would be a helpful and commonly used feature, but then remembers “we’re Apple! We simply have to be overly-niche and off the beaten path and unique!”.

The standing tracker is still dead worthless. By 10am I typically get the notification that I’ve been standing for 8 hours while barely out of bed for 4, and I don’t even wear the watch to bed. I don’t like that I had to go on an expedition of googling how to turn off announcements and notifications in the middle of my sessions, they just interrupt whatever I’m listening to/focusing on and they shouldn’t be turned on by default. 

It’s annoying that I have to go into “step metrics” just to get a loose idea of how many steps I took on a run. I have no idea why they don’t automatically include it with the session details, but once again, Apple just insists on being different like that’s the only thing that matters. 

Overall, glad they finally recognized weight lifting as an exercise. Still doesn’t outweigh that this is a bottom-of-the-pack fitness tracker.

2026 - Update

author: Fiery Bobo

title: exactly what I needed
body:
This app has helped me get back into a regular fitness routine after a difficult moment in my life. I’ve used fitness+ for over 4 years. It may sound cheesy but, on hard days, it feels really good to have a trainer motivate you through a workout. I appreciate how trainers on Apple Fitness+ treat workouts as physical and mental endeavors that one should be proud of for doing. 

The variety of workouts you can do is AMAZING! Great if you want to mix things up or if, you know, are quick to judge your improvements for one type of exercise and need to try something else for a while. 

The music used to bother me but then I learned that you can filter by type - and that they’re always adding more! I love the new J Pop and K Pop!! More more more!!!! It’s always such a sweet surprise when I pick a new workout and it’s themed after a month or a celebration. As someone in both LGBTQ and AAPI communities, I really love how inclusive the trainers and the workouts can be. Gyms can be much less forgiving…and wildly expensive!!

Because the app keeps a nice record of what you’ve done over time it’s easy to see that something has dramatically changed in how the app tracks your progress. title: Don’t believe the sub-3 stars
body:
So I’ve been using Beachbody on Demand, or BODi as it has become, for almost a decade now, and full disclosure: I cannot recommend that platform enough! It is AMAZING, BUT the price has become absolutely out of control.

That led me to try Apple Fitness, not only is it possible to get a three free month trial, but subscriptions are around half the price of BODi. The cardio workouts are  absolutely phenomenal, I was unsure at first because I like a pretty extreme amount of difficulty. And these, while feeling familiar, are a good challenge!

People are complaining that it doesn’t properly add on steps or something? Who cares! Do you really need an app’s validation for your fitness to count? No dear reader, you are smarter than that! My only critique (and maybe they will add this in the future) is entire strength programs, where weekly you could work through major muscle groups with home equipment like BODi has. But don’t let that stop you from trying out Apple Fitness!

title: Workouts are great, needs work elsewhere
body:
I love the workouts and instructors but the overall user experience feels half baked.

I would love to see some social proofing that shows if other users liked/disliked the workout. Maybe a “users typically burn 15% more calories with this workout.” Something to highlight what I’m getting into from the user’s perspective. I’m not looking for community necessarily, I just want to be prepared for what Anja is about to do to me.

I would love a summary of stats for the workouts I keep in my library (if they’ve been completed), it would help me keep track of which ones were high calorie burners and which ones we’re challenging in other ways. Avg cals, avg HR, plus highest/lowest of those ranges.

No way to categorize the library by type of workout, duration, etc. A tagging system at bare minimum so I could quickly see my highest cal workouts for example. Just a wild choice to only have that as an endlessly scrolling list, very under developed part of then experience.

I WOULD LOVE to be able to see my stats when I’m casting to my MacBook or TV. I workout so much this way. Just put the stats on the screen, stop gatekeeping them behind certain products or situations and start thinking more inclusively/globally about how people use your product. Doing a HIIT workout from a phone screen is really hard to see. I know you want me to buy an Apple TV for this but alternatively you can chose to treat your users better.

If you need a director of product on the team I’d be happy to help.

title: It could be so much better
body:
I really want to like the fitness app, but it’s severely lacking in some core ways. 

The good:
I love the fitness rings. They’re the core functionality of Apple Fitness, and they’re a great way of staying on top of basic daily fitness goals.

The bad:
Advanced Fitness Tracking sucks on Apple fitness. Beyond the rings and very basic workout tracking (name of workout & duration) there’s almost nothing here. Why not let me track specific exercises, reps, splits, PRs, etc? I want to track my pushups, bench press max, 5k and marathon PR, etc. Instead I just get a generic “outdoor run” with a duration, or other generic workouts which lack useful metrics. 

The ugly:
Fitness+ is one of the most tone-deaf things they could have done with Apple Fitness. They’re basically selling all excitement with no substance. At first I was excited about the “custom plans”, but the plans are limited to the few workout categories they’ve produced videos for. So to actually use a “custom plan” I have to adjust my workout style into their narrow and kind of weird categories (mindful cooldown??). Custom plans are almost useless. 

Most of fitness plus is just videos of fake-excited trainers with pasted on smiles telling me how to do very basic exercises. It’s all very flashy, but mostly a waste of time and money. 

I want to live Apple Fitness. Give me something useful!

author: Steve3465

title: So much potential missed!
body:
Apple Fitness, paired with an  Apple watch, has so much potential, but right now it feels like a missed opportunity.

Where this app really falls short is in camaraderie, competition, and motivation. Other fitness platforms have figured out how powerful community can be. Weekly, monthly, and annual challenges. Team competitions. Badges, milestones, and real incentives to stay consistent. These are the features that actually keep people moving, and Apple is barely scratching the surface.

There is little sense of friendly competition or accountability. You cannot easily participate in meaningful group challenges, long-term streak competitions, or seasonal goals with friends the way you can on apps like Myzone® or Peloton. Those platforms make fitness feel social, fun, and addictive in the best way. Apple Fitness, by comparison, feels isolated and flat.

I was also disappointed that there was no real “Year in Review.” Many fitness and lifestyle apps now provide an annual recap that celebrates your progress, milestones, and consistency. It is motivating, shareable, and helps users reflect on how far they have come. Apple completely missed that opportunity.

Apple has the data, the ecosystem, and the user base to be the undisputed leader in fitness tracking. But right now, it falls far short of what is possible. If Apple took cues from platforms like Myzone® and Peloton and leaned into challenges, community, and yearly progress storytelling, this could easily become the best fitness app on the market. Instead, it feels like a basic tracker with very little soul.

title: Calendar Based Metrics Are Not Helpful - use Sliding
body:
This app needs sliding window metrics, 7-days, 30-days, 90-days and 365-days. These would make sense.

The Calendar-Based metrics are very unhelpful. Humans do not effectively adjust behaviors on arbitrary dates, they do it based on history trends. Showing only 1 day of history as soon as a new month or year has begun makes it a useless metric.

Any time you change behavior it should immediately stand out as deviating from trend. Current app hides trend… why?

Using “Workouts” on Apple Watch is inconsistent and glitchy, and changes without warning—not the kind of surprise you want when you’re about to start the day’s workout. Especially when planning workouts or viewing data, it’s significantly lacking in so many ways, and seems like it’s only targeted at casual users (couch to 5k types). It’s difficult to believe any of the product owners or engineers working on this use it for advanced training (marathon builds, etc.), are serious athletes themselves, or have done the bare minimum of R&D to understand how inadequate this is when compared to competing products (Garmin, Coros, Polar, etc.).

title: Needs improvement
body: Why do they make workout visualizations so different, during a workout, and post workout read out? Why can’t I see my time in a segment during HIIT, but can see it during cross training (on my watch and phone)? At least now you can configure a workout on your phone, but it’s still easier to use a 3rd party app for this. On notifications during workouts…one should be easily able to stop certain types via settings, including obvious ones like ‘hey you reached your exercise goal for the day’. In-session notifications like segment duration last too long. Finally, queues during workouts should be configurable. If I have a custom run and start running too slow I get a good vibration on my watch, but that’s not the case when you get back into the pre configured rythm, the vibration is no where near as strong and not very noticeable if trying to run fast. title: Fairly Accurate On Steps, Horrifically Inaccurate In Calorie Count
body: So, as someone that has been on both sides of the isle, not being able to lose weight and losing too much weight, this app is odd. It counts calories at what seems like a discounted rate, I haven’t been updating my measurements but they aren’t too out of date. 6’2 and 179lbs, with a 30,603 steps down, that is or at least should be 1,200 calories burned, to this app it’s barely under 800. While it doesn’t seem like a huge amount, I can imagine less knowledgeable on their height and weight base burn and the amount of additional energy cost needed while being taller to do those kind of numbers getting discouraged by the numbers not reflecting the amount of work put in, quitting all together. That isn’t and has never been the goal for fitness, in fact it should only be to cultivate a split that works best for the individual. I know having an 800 calorie burn goal is obsessive, but I couldn’t imagine someone having a normal 500 calorie step goal, you’d probably need 20k steps minimum to make such a goal, and for context that’s about 8.5 to 10 MILES. That’s about one and a half times a walk through the FULL Central Park loop. I don’t know how they’ve messed up the math here, but they definitely have.

Support link just takes me to a selection of articles that do not discuss this problem and are of no use. When I go to delete app it warns I will lose my history (which seems strange considering all of Apple’s other cloud-based integrations through iCloud), although I’m almost at the point of doing so because Fitness+ has little utility for me without custom plans (I’m not going to search for every single workout I do, will just work out on my own at that point or use some other app).

title: Just a few more tweaks would make it perfect.
body:
This is a no-brainer for me. 

I used to wake up at 5 AM every day, drive to the gym, oftentimes fighting inclement weather in my slowly-awakening state. Upon arriving, I needed to change my shoes, stuff my items into a cubby or a locker, and then claim an ideal spot on the floor for my HIIT style of lesson. Sometimes the music was good, sometimes it was awful and I just had to deal with it. After all was said and done, I needed to drive home dripping sweat into my car, rush to shower, so that I could then start work on time. This app eliminates that entire routine. 

Now I can simply roll out of bed, turn on my tv, and work out in my boxers. Same quality experience for 1/6 of the price I was paying for the gym. The only thing I miss is that my gym had a floating floor. The bounce and cushioning of that floor was hard to leave behind.

This app boasts a variety of quality trainers. I avoid workouts with some of them, but I’ve definitely found my favorites (Jessica - Yoga, Kyle - Strength and Core, Gregg - Core, Jenn - Core, Darryl - Pilates, Sam - Core). 
The ability to stack workouts is appreciated. I enjoy listening to the variety of music, and if I really enjoy something, I will add it to my favorites in the Apple Music app.

Workouts are easy to search. Whether it’s searching by trainer, length, equipment or no equipment, duration, everything is easy to navigate.

However, there are 3 additions I would greatly appreciate that would make this app perfect.

1.) Create a search function for workouts focusing on a body part. I understand strength usually will have exercises for the arms, but I want to be more specific. Biceps, triceps, chest, shoulders, etc. Categorize workouts that focus on a specific muscle group, and enable users to search via those filters. My shoulder strength leaves a lot to be desired. 

2.) While the app does offer cooldowns, similar to my request above, I want there to be sessions dedicated to not only pre and post workout stretch routines, but also make said sessions searchable by body part/muscle group. Yoga does wonders for stretching, but I wish I had more of a focused approach when I’m feeling tight in certain areas.

3.) Trainer profiles. I’d like to know more about the trainers and their backgrounds. It goes a long way in making up for the connection one might lose from no longer attending a gym. Granted, I do not want to encourage para-social relationship building as that can create privacy and even safety concerns in the weird world we live in, but just an intro interview of who the trainer is and their backgrounds, followed by maybe a monthly interview of what physical activities they’ve been engaged in lately, or diets they’re following, or just motivational tips one can watch between workouts. What motivates them? What are their workouts? How much can Kyle bench?
I read up on Kyle’s background and his college football experience, as well as Darryl’s pro experience. Jessica’s surf background is unique for people that do not live on the west coast. Sam’s affinity for running is something that I didn’t initially know, and just created a little more of a connection for me since I am also a runner. It’s just interesting to know and helps develop a little bit better of a connection, which aids motivation.

title: Good, but not Apple Excellence
body:
This app is fantastic it delivers a standard well above what’s currently on the market. It’s engaging, fun, and promotes a healthy lifestyle. The Awards keep me motivated, the tracking features are improving, and the insights have been invaluable I’ve learned a lot about my sleep and athletic performance.

Paired with my Apple Watch, this app has empowered me to take control of my fitness, track my progress, and stay organized. One of the best parts is that I was able to share my data with my doctor, who used it to address health concerns and demonstrate to my health insurance company that I’ve been putting in the work.

Here’s how this app could reach an even higher level of excellence: add food tracking. Specifically, let me use my iPhone to log my protein, fat, and other nutritional goals. I’m not asking for dietary advice just the ability to scan a UPC code and track my food intake to help me stay aligned with my goals. Done with Apple’s signature simplicity, intuitiveness, and friendly interface, this would be a true game changer in helping users make healthier eating decisions, especially with their already built award system.

Likewise with golfing, I want to see an accurate counting of the time from start to finish with the activity and an update could include whether one is walking a course or using a cart, as well as how many holes. I would also like to see how many steps were taken doing this activity.

title: One Star – Great Workouts Trapped in a Garbage App
body:
Apple Fitness+ has some solid workouts and likable instructors — too bad they’re buried under one of the worst user interfaces I’ve ever experienced. Navigating this app feels like Apple actively wants you to give up on exercising.

There’s no way to build a program or plan your week. You can’t filter by difficulty, progression, or even mark favorites properly. Want to resume where you left off? Good luck — this thing has the memory of a goldfish. And don’t even get me started on syncing issues. Half the time my Apple Watch stats don’t show up, or the app just freezes altogether.

It’s shocking how bad this is coming from a company known for sleek design. Fitness+ feels like it was slapped together by interns on a deadline, then forgotten. Great workouts, absolutely sabotaged by a lazy, frustrating, joyless user experience. Apple should be embarrassed.

title: Three star well deserved
body:
As much as I do love the app and everything that does to help me track my fitness, I feel like it’s missing quite a few major components that could make reviewing the workout more beneficial for the user. 

For any distance based activity, the only way to find out the top speed is to go into the workout details, click “show more” and then clicking “15 min” selection. Only then can you see your top speed for biking, running etc. This information should be included on the “Workout Details“ section-especially without having to adjust the time segment to see the ACTUAL top speed. As a training cyclist, this is very important to me. 

The second feature I think would be excellent is to introduce a more triathlon style of switching workouts at my own pace without setting any Schedule before hand and losing current progress of an activity. My city has exercise gym equipment at various parks and I sporadically like to stop and do some repetitions for a few minutes during running or cycling. What this does to my full work out review at the end of the day is divided up my biking segments and my workout segments instead of showing it all lumped together with one number for each workout.  

Lastly, one feature that I think would be nice is an easy edit for workout segments. There are times after a long bike ride that I forget to turn off the exercise and it continues to record me while I’m driving home. It would be nice if I could just trim that time as easily as I can edit a video in the photo app.

If these features get implemented, I’ll change my review to five stars. I honestly do love the app and what it does for tracking, but some of the inconveniences are annoying.

title: So much potential
body: I want to love this app. I really do. Its best feature is the ring. The satisfaction that comes with spinning it is unparalleled. It’s second best feature is the fact that it plugs directly into Apple’s health app. However, therein lies a fault because it takes forever to show your progress. In a world of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Bionic chipsets, there’s absolutely no reason why there can’t be real time updates. And with what we pay for these devices, we shouldn’t have to wait on our phones to do anything. One last fail, is the inability to challenge friends to custom challenges. Something as simple as spinning a ring once for the day; spinning a ring twice for the day; spinning a ring twice for the day for three days, five days, seven days straight. Custom, in every meaning of the word, or at least most. I know it’s impossible to make everyone happy, but this app could be so much more than it is, and the Apple DEV team owes it to its consumers to put in the work and brain power to make it happen.

title: Needs so much work :/
body: The activity rings are sooooo close to uselessness. There really needs to be a toggle to remove stand hours, and a toggle to change the calorie goal to only count calories burned from intentional movement from workouts (sorry, calories burned in the course of daily living aren’t metabolically the same as intentional exercise, totally different kind of bioenergy recruitment involved). Exercise ring  minutes are virtually irrelevant. Why not count intentional exercise minutes over the course of a week? Why no option to set a custom day period? And no, I don’t mean the scheduling option. Motivation, will to exercise, ability and subjective strength can vary from day to day for a bajillion reasons. Track totals by weekly periods and make them customizable! It’s just not useful to be restricted to scheduling the ring goals by set days of the week as if they are calendar deadlines! Also takes way too many taps to view workouts and workout data.

title: Love the app but….
body:
There have been quite a few times that I have pulled up the app and been unable to play a video, or while I’m working out the video pauses and buffers before knocking off all together. This, especially, is frustrating because oftentimes I am halfway or further through the work out and have to start over. There isn’t a fast forward option or an option to pick up where you left off. I’m not able to just start over, I have time constraints which is why I built my custom plans in the app. 

Also, even though I have selected the trainers I prefer, I still keep getting videos by the ones I don’t particularly like which makes it hard to enjoy the video or get the most out of it. 

Aside from those things, the premise of the app is amazing and I love it when it works. I think the price point is very fair too, hard to find a fair price when everyone wants to price gouge for everything.

title: Finally reaching my goals!

I already have some of my favorite trainers saved to my library. I am simply blown away by how fun and upbeat these workouts have been for me. Took nearly 90 minutes to stop sweating and cool down. So yeah, I KNOW I should have logged at least 20 minutes of exercise. I used to have a fitbit before this and I hate to say it (not really), but the app for fitbit was nearly 100% customizable (not to mention a 100% complete app). This is my first Apple Watch (9 series) & it’s cute I guess, but for the price I find it excessively restrictive & expensive to buy all the apps necessary to customize things correctly.

title: How to become an exercise master
body:
In order to preserve your sanity, I highly suggest you immediately change the number of minutes required to close the exercise ring to the minimum of 5 and here’s why:

After using this app for nearly a year, it has become increasingly clear that Apple does not take this measurement seriously, so neither should you in regards to the exercise ring. Instead marvel with wonder on how you can get exercise minutes by…
1. Driving your car!
2. Typing on a keyboard!
3. Sitting on the couch watching TV!
4. Not wearing the watch at all!

(I did not start a workout for any of these activities, FYI.)

Meanwhile, here’s what won’t give you the exercise minutes to close your ring:
1. Walking 5 miles in a day. 
2. Loading and unloading trucks for several hours.
3. Climbing stairs. 

So yeah, don’t overdo yourself because your exercise didn’t fit Apple’s Calvinballesque definition. Just stay active and keep working at it.

body:
Raise your hand if your name is Juliana and you went to Starbucks today.

title: Love the Fitness app! Every update gets better!
body:

This latest update and I’m even cancelling Gentler — the Load card is the quick, intuitive view needed to quickly adjust my intensity in any given day to stay in a good progressive, productive improvement track and not overdo (which I sort of love to do - lol!)
    for context, I’m 66F, have worked out/lifted for 30+ years. While unfortunately always second priority to work, the workouts have always come back after seasons of overdoing at work and are a foundation. I got sooo much more consistent with the Apple Watch and now the data is reducing need for other apps. Nice work!!

body: I love these workouts, I love the trainers and the programs, and I love the flexibility it provides for me to workout at home. But, man, the glitches are huge frustrations for me. title: Wow. Truly impressive. I can see the innovation at work here.
body:
Used for about 6-7 months maybe more, work out 5 times a week and the issues with this app make me not even want to use it and I’ve avoided workouts because of how awful this is. I don’t understand how difficult it is to create a program get it to a functional level and then just stop screwing with it. This fitness program started out as an amazing thing that tracked so many different metrics and multiples ways to complete wide range of work outs, and was so seamlessly integrated with the Watch and the AirPod pros and the phone and Apple TV at first and has turned into an absolute nightmare to use that makes me not even want to work out. I have major connectivity issues between all of my Apple devices while using this app the devices do not consistently track or record the metrics. The metrics are inconsistently reported and recorded, and then extrapolated by the app giving unsupportive results and trends that you then have to go back and manually fix yourself or just accept  none of your data is accurate and the “fitness trends” mean nothing. 

Workouts no longer seamlessly interact on the phone and the watch. I’ve had multiple workouts that I started on the phone and then my watch continued to start the workout, but the phone never actually initiated the workout and then as soon as I open my phone again, it’s suspended my workout, which then I have to close the program down, completely canceled the entire workout then start all over with a new workout. Now I’ve got broken metrics that aren’t actually reflective of the reality of my health which completely undermine the entire purpose of every part of these metrics. 

As if that wasn’t truly thrilling enough all of the walk and run workouts with the subscription  you can no longer initiate an outdoor walk. It will always start as a treadmill workout which then my phone watch and app cuts out 50% of the metrics that are supposed to be actually counted. 

Started a walking workout on my phone, which then automatically started the workout on my watch like it’s supposed to. What it’s not supposed to do is start a workout on my watch while suspending the workout in my phone so that I have the same workout in two different phases on two different devices with no notifications no or alerts. Got zero credit or metrics for about 15 minutes of walking this afternoon. Had to stop my workout twice mid workout just to try to fix this app.

Yet again, truly innovative here, when you start a workout on your phone and then try to continue the workout on your Apple TV. It only works about half the time the sound doesn’t consistently play through then you have a four second window to find the Apple TV remote while your mid workout so you can press a button to then redirect the audio on your Apple TV to your AirPod pros that have been in the entire time. If you miss that one pop up, that only appears about 1/4 of the time, then you’re done it will never come up again and there is no way to manually do this. I have yet out of 10 workouts been able to consistently get this to function so that I can actually use the AirPods that I paid to use while using the system to work out that I actually also pay for.

I’ve Cancelled this subscription and am looking to any other phone brand moving forward. I’ve had Apple devices for 20 years and regret getting suckered into this and I regret selling as many as I did while I university. I will literally pay my family to use any other fitness platform than this, that’s how upset, frustrated and irritated I am about the absolute regression of almost everything Apple touches into nonfunctional goblins that have a premium price tag on them.

title: Great workouts, wide variety of options
body:
Update:
Please add the ability to comment personally on workouts. If I didn’t like a routine, then I’d like to leave myself a note to not repeat it at a later date. 

Original review: 
I have been using the app for over 2 years now and can vastly see an increase for my motivation to workout using this app. 
Suggestions to developers would be to allow saving of ‘favorite’ workouts that you would be able to rate and/or write comments about. For example: being able to list the weight that was used in the routine in order to measure increases in strength the next time the routine gets completed. I have been creating my own version of this feature by saving stacks with my weights listed in the title of the stack name. 
Another suggestion would be to allow the programmed routine for the plan to automatically continue to the next exercise in the day’s plan, the way that the stack feature prompts to continue. 

Love the additions and hope to see increased features for targeting specific exercises. Overall love how the plan seems to group similar movements together for body part specific targets. The pilates with strength training tends to use similar movements that help emphasize the routine.

title: A Frustrating Mix of Motivation and Glitches
body:
Apple Fitness+ has the potential to be a fantastic motivator. The app gamifies exercise with colorful badges and rewards, making fitness fun and engaging. It's a great way to encourage people to stay active and reach their goals. However, persistent glitches in the app are undermining this positive experience.

The most frustrating issue is a bug that randomly erases move awards. All that hard work and commitment can vanish in an instant, leaving users feeling discouraged and demotivated. It's incredibly disheartening to see your progress erased, and it makes it difficult to stay motivated to exercise.

While Apple Fitness+ has some great features, these glitches are a major drawback. The app needs a serious update to fix these issues and ensure that users' hard work is recognized and rewarded. Until then, it's difficult to recommend the app wholeheartedly.

title: I Want to Love It
body:
Sustain:  

I love the social aspect I have with my family and friends who have Apple Watches.  It is the only reason I feel the need to use my Apple Watch over my Suunto or Garmin watches.  That said, I have some ideas for improvement in the event Apple actually takes feedback from consumers.

Improve:  

I love the ability to compete with my friends who have Apple Watches but it needs more customization capability.  My “opponents” often give up after failing to meet one day and although the workout should be their true prize, blah, blah, blah, I think it is a missed opportunity to help them succeed.  Daily competitions that allow more than 600 points would solve this problem instead of always having to settle for the we both win result.  Yes everyone wins if we are striving to be healthy,  but some actually want to compete against our friends and family because it is fun to push ourselves to achieve more.  Additionally, monthly competitions would also be a great motivator  to encourage sustained effort over longer periods instead of “losing” over one day because you were busy with life’s expected and unexpected events.

I would also love to see a feature to add workouts that feature added weights such as weighted vests or ruck marches that increase calorie consumption based on the added weight.  In the era of functional fitness, CrossFit, and the multitude of ways people are staying fit, it seems like an important and easy solution to keep long time Apple product users such as myself interested.

title: Would recommend
body:
I have used this app for several years, as it syncs with the numerous Apple products that my family uses. I love the diversity of trainers and their engaging and efficient workouts. I would recommend adding workouts tailored for the elliptical machine and also workouts tailored for kids, to get them involved in fitness early. 
Another suggestion is to allow an exercise video to play on multiple Apple devices at the same time.  Example: for yoga videos, sometimes I have to look towards the ground, or to the side, and I would prefer to glance at my Apple Watch or phone that is more conveniently positioned instead of the TV or computer I started the video on. 

I intermittently get issues with the app connecting to my watch or phone, but this may be based on Wi-Fi connectivity and not the app. 

Overall, would highly recommend.

title: A great tool for your fitness journey
body:
I absolutely love this app! There are always new workouts so you never grow tired of starting the same routine over and over. The coach’s are filled positivity helping to make each workout feel empowering. And the ability to have a small bit of control over what music you listen to is nice, although I wish there was more. It would be nice to create your own playlist to workout to or more music style options. There is also a good variety of workout styles to select from. I have been enjoying the strength training and cycling options on the days I workout at home. The yoga videos are amazing replacements for the days the yoga studio I attend is closed. 

I want to give it a 5 but am giving it a very strong 4 as I don’t think many of the workouts are beginner friendly. I wouldn’t say anything is extremely advanced but as an example, I’m new to cycling and would love a way to build my endurance without randomly selecting a cycling workout and hoping for the best. It would be nice to have a way to filter easy vs hard workouts or have some indication of beginner, moderate, advanced levels. I have definitely learned that a workout is not any easier because it is 10 minutes vs a longer 20+ minute option.

title: The music ruins it—just add more options!
body: Could be a really cool app, but even with the new trainer/music audio focus, there’s no way to escape the default playlists. Downloaded the app because my favorite yoga teacher moved here, but without being able to turn off the curated playlists, there’s no way to drop into a meditative space and fully connect with my own inner experience. How can I listen to my body and assess my mental and emotional state when the practice has a built-in “vibe” that’s intended to manufacture feelings externally, instead of honoring what’s present internally? People practice yoga in many ways and for many reasons—please consider those of us who prefer to practice without music. Many platforms include music as an optional feature for yoga and workouts, which is great, because everyone has different preferences! Having the ability to choose to practice in silence, select my own music, or, at the very least, opt for a more neutral playlist, something ambient or without lyrics, is an essential feature.

title: Good app, but I have a few suggestions.
body: I’ve been using Fitness+ for several years.  I enjoy most of the workouts.  I especially like the fact that I can see my stats (heart rate, calories, etc.) while I’m working out.  I do have a few suggestions to improve the app.  (1) I’m a musician and I find it frustrating that the strength workouts never follow the beat of the music. My assumption is that Apple is trying to advertise Apple Music.  The product would be better if the music was chosen to enhance the exercise instead of the other way around.  (2) The introductions to the workouts are downright silly, something like: “First we’re going to do something and then something else and then we’ll repeat that three times”.  Tell me what muscles are being targeted or at least the name of the exercises we’ll be doing.  (3) I was looking forward to the dance routines, but they are too hard (and the Senior dance routines are too easy).  (4) The cooldowns in the strength videos are way too short, which would be ok, if the Mindful Cooldown videos were more comprehensive.  I end up making up my own cooldown routines, but I would rather follow an instructor.

title: Love Apple Fitness—please add a trans trainer!
body:
I’ve been using Apple Fitness workouts consistently since the beginning of the pandemic and find it to be better than anything  else available on the market and for a fraction of the price. When I travel for work and have other equipment available, there’s a workout to correspond (rowing, stationary bike, etc). But I can always sneak in a 30 min strength workout no matter I am or what equipment is available. Would love to see a 45 min strength option in the upper/lower/total body sections.

Beyond the practical review is the quality and diversity of trainers—I love that Jenn has been added to the strength crew, increasing the number of women of color trainers. I really appreciate the celebration and inclusion of a variety of cultures and identities throughout the months and years—it’s part of why I have stuck with the app this long.

My hope is that Apple is ready to add a trainer who is openly transgender. As an LGBT athlete, I’ve appreciated how many openly gay trainers there are on the Fitness Plus Team but it’s been almost four years now without a trans trainer and I’m scratching my head about this, given how many trans trainers there are in the U.S. and abroad. 

Keep up the great work and thanks for putting out such a great product for those of us committed to an inclusive and diverse idea of fitness.

My biggest issue is with using my Apple TV to stream the workouts. (I’ve tried the app on the Apple TV instead, but it crashes and glitches even worse, often repeatedly losing the connection to my Apple Watch.) When streaming, the workouts sometimes crash the app completely and I often have to start over rather than being asked if I’d like to resume the workout. Lately, this has been  less frequent. Instead, the audio will play from both my iPhone and the TV or not at all; the workout pauses or skips (usually only a few seconds, but annoying); and using the stack never, ever works as it should. With the stack, the next workout will not play, will crash, or the audio comes from the phone while the screen looks like it should for streaming! I’ve played and played with all of this and cannot make it work. 
I like most of the trainers, the on screen metrics, etc. However, the social justice comments supporting various people groups and especially LGBT+ are obnoxious and pushy. I refuse to start any workout that was published in June and try to ignore it all, but it drives me crazy.

title: Apple Fitness+: An Exceptional Platform That Could Use a Pregnancy Fitness Section
body:
As a dedicated user of Apple Fitness+, I've found it to be an outstanding platform that seamlessly integrates into my daily routine. The variety of workouts, from high-energy HIIT sessions to calming yoga classes, caters to diverse fitness levels and interests. The seamless integration with Apple Watch provides real-time feedback and personalized metrics, enhancing the overall experience and motivation.

One aspect I particularly appreciate is the wide variety of the content library. The trainers are not only knowledgeable but also engaging, creating a sense of community and encouragement. The ability to filter workouts by duration, type, and even music genre makes it easy to find the perfect session for any mood or schedule.

However, while Apple Fitness+ excels in many areas, I feel it would greatly benefit from adding a dedicated section for pregnancy fitness. Pregnancy is a unique time in a woman's life, and tailored fitness options are crucial for maintaining health and well-being. Specialized workouts that address the different stages of pregnancy, focusing on safe and effective exercises, would provide immense value to expectant mothers. 

Thank you,

For the plans, I wish I could delete & add some of my favorite workouts. For instance, I made a plan, but I really want to include the strength workout featuring Daft Punk. I can’t find a way to delete one 20 minute workout and add in another one of my choice. 3. I think the whole Health & Fitness apps really need some updating. You should be able to edit your workout, like the start and end times for when you forget, or the distance of a run when you are on a treadmill or do a measured track but the watch records it incorrectly. 4. I wish you could fast forward and rewind in the workout. I know that might make things difficult since it syncs to your Apple Watch, but it’s annoying when you have two workouts in a day, but both workouts spend 3 minutes doing a warmup. I don’t always need to warmup for my second workout but there’s no way to skip it.5. Sometimes the app refuses to connect to my Apple Watch - I think that’s probably the glitch I’ve encountered the most often.

title: Repetitive
body:
Fitness + is good for people who are new to exercise or have no idea how to plan workouts. However the plan option is not what I thought it would be. Essentially you create your own plan with some prompts. This is good but then all the videos are so repetitive they really miss potential for increased benefit. For example all of the strength videos I have done include squats, rows, and hinges but rarely lunges and never hip thrusts, weighted bridges, or lateral pulls. The modifications are always “smaller range” which is not instructive at all and misses the potential for key movement shifts to build toward the intended movement. There is virtually no cueing or alignment instructions which can quite negatively impact a person who has little clue on how to self cue. 

The yoga and Pilates are also extremely limited with very little variation which is crazy because there is so much to yoga and Pilates to create infinite workouts. Instead it seems heavy on repetitions (again NO cueing) and largely focused toward big muscle groups, neglecting the extremely important supporting muscles. Furthermore, it appears the instructors are not really educated in proper technique as the sequencing for both Pilates and yoga doesn’t allow for a healthy transition from stillness to full body range. There are SO many more yoga poses and Pilates moves that are completely absent. I wouldn’t consider either of these practices taught by well educated practitioners. YouTube is far superior here - and free! 

And all the warmups are basically not there. 60 seconds of some low squats and a few arm circles is highly inadequate and injury very likely eventually will occur. 

I gave this a solid 2 months of near daily workouts to form this opinion. I do not recommend this app for those brand new to fitness OR those people well established in fitness. It’s really only good for the middle ground folks or perhaps returning to fitness after a break but even then the warmup is not sufficient. 

I wanted to love this. 😔

Rather than being marked as standing for 6 hours I was marked for standing for 2 hours or even 30 minutes for the in day. author: AlyxLynn

title: Total fail
body: Did you miss part of the instructions from the trainer? Too bad rewind is not an option. Are they doing an exercise you can’t do? Can’t skip ahead, no fast-forward allowed. Looking for a specific workout in your saved workouts? With no folders or filters to help store and search your saved workouts you just gotta dig through until you find it. The entire Apple Fitness platform is a failure for forcing its rigid interface onto users rather than allowing us to have control over our fitness experience. If it’s not a live class I should be able to rewind and fast forward and change the audio to whatever I want. Would you rather listen to a podcast or audiobook rather than the cringe inducing drivel being spouted by the spin instructors? Well, you can’t. It’s the cheesiest, dumbest monologue you’ll ever have the displeasure of sweating to. The best you can do is mute it and pair your AirPods to a different device which is the only thing that keeps me from flinging my iPad across the room every time the spin instructor compares the class to a music festival or some such nonsense. It would also be extremely helpful, especially for the hearing impaired, to have clear instructions displayed on the screen - not subtitles of what the instructor is saying (90% of which is garbage) but simple prompts to increase intensity or stand up, etc. Yes you can watch what the instructor is doing but sometimes it’s hard to tell especially when you have the audio turned off. This probably wouldn’t be an option for other apple fitness workouts but when doing something repetitive like spin it makes total sense. Do better Apple.

This is my particular complaint but it leads to a more general and more important one. ⬇️

Your fitness app really shows your biases through the images featured and the types of workouts included about who you think does or should workout. 😠 Many people with mobility constraints, or who are older, or who carry more weight are indeed working out. Some of them, while not included in your photography, could still use your included fitness routine trackers. Try visiting a community center or retirement community (instead of fancy gyms) to learn more. Do better please.

title: So much potential, in a much needed field!
body:
Apple's Fitness App, despite being embedded within the ecosystem of one of the world's most innovative technology companies, paradoxically seems to have missed the mark in fully captivating its audience. In a sphere where Apple has consistently set the standard for user experience and engagement, the Fitness App notably lacks the polish and motivational prowess we've come to expect from the brand's offerings.

The app undoubtedly holds significant potential, serving as a gateway for Apple enthusiasts to engage with their health and fitness goals in a more integrated and Apple-centric manner. However, it falls short in delivering the innovative features and captivating experiences that could make it a cornerstone of the Apple ecosystem. The absence of a significant overhaul or meaningful updates to the Fitness App is a missed opportunity, especially considering the growing global emphasis on health and wellness.

One might argue that, for a company that has revolutionized personal computing, mobile communications, and wearable technology, there exists a surprising oversight in not applying the same level of ambition and innovation towards enhancing its fitness application. This is particularly perplexing when considering the app's potential to serve not just as a tool for tracking physical activity, but as a platform for inspiring and motivating its user base towards healthier lifestyles.

To truly resonate with its fans and stand out in the crowded fitness app market, Apple's Fitness App would benefit from a comprehensive revamp. Such an update should not only address user interface and experience improvements but also introduce a range of engaging and personalized features. Imagine a version of the app that leverages AI to tailor workout recommendations, incorporates social features for added motivation, and offers interactive challenges that make fitness fun and engaging. By doing so, Apple could significantly increase the app's appeal and effectiveness, turning it into yet another reason for consumers to stay within its ecosystem.

In conclusion, while the Apple Fitness App harbors the potential to be a pivotal element in the tech giant's suite of services, it requires a substantial injection of the innovation and user-focused design Apple is known for. An overhaul could transform it from a mere utility to an essential, motivating companion for individuals looking to lead healthier lives. It's time for Apple to apply its renowned magic touch to its Fitness App, much like it does with every new launch, to truly motivate and inspire its dedicated fan base.

I hope to see this app change!!

title: suggestions for Apple Fitness+
body:
I’ve been comparing Apple Fitness+ with the plethora of workout videos available on YouTube, and I’ve noticed a significant difference in engagement. While Apple Fitness+ offers quality workouts, the repetitive scenery of their Apple Fitness Studio, along with the trainers’ less varied attire, falls short in keeping my interest peaked. On the other hand, YouTube fitness creators bring their workouts to life with vibrant backgrounds—ranging from serene swimming pools to lush gardens—and often incorporate elements like pets, which adds a personal touch that’s sorely missing in the more sterile environment of Apple Fitness+.

Furthermore, the personalities of YouTube trainers shine through their videos, making each workout feel like a unique experience rather than a routine session. These creators are adept at crafting their on-screen personas, making workouts feel more like an engaging TV show than a mere exercise video. Their instructions are not only more detailed, providing specific advice on what to do and what to avoid, but also offer variations for all levels, making fitness accessible to everyone.

Additionally, Apple Fitness+ could take inspiration from YouTube’s thematic approach to workout videos. Creators can utilize themes—be it colors like red, blue, yellow, or orange, or specific aesthetics—to match the vibe of the workout, enhancing the viewer’s emotional and visual experience. This thematic variation not only adds a layer of excitement but also helps in setting the right mood for different types of workouts. Incorporating such elements into Apple Fitness+ could significantly enrich the user experience, making each workout feel fresh and tailored to the mood or energy level one seeks.

By integrating more diverse backdrops, thematic elements, and allowing trainers to express their unique personalities, Apple Fitness+ could transform workout sessions into a more immersive and engaging journey, akin to a vibrant TV show that viewers can’t wait to tune into.

title: Sneaky Subscription Traps + Terrible Support from Apple
body:
I got a free trial of this app from Best Buy. It was fun (and I love how each class uses sign language) but I never used it enough to justify a subscription. When the trial ended, Apple started charging me for the app, so I submitted a dispute for the charges. 

Apple wouldn’t refund me. I even called Apple Support and spoke to a specialist then a senior specialist. They both said they couldn’t do anything due to “Apple policy” but they weren’t even able to explain their policy. So, I looked it up…

It states, “From time to time, Apple may suspend or cancel payment or refuse a refund request if we find evidence of fraud, abuse, or unlawful or other manipulative behavior that entitles Apple to a corresponding counterclaim.”

The only unlawful, abusive, manipulative behavior is the unethical actions of Apple. 

Apple Support trains their specialists to be bullies—not to understand their own policies. 

It’s not like the subscription cost will “break my bank account,” but so many unnecessary subscriptions add up and Apple isn’t handling this situation (and others, I imagine) ethically.

title: Motivating app, glitches are frustrating
body: I have completed 100+ trainer led workouts in the last 7 weeks. I have enjoyed the variety of trainers, workouts, and music. This app has motivated me to stick to my goals and create a life changing routine that I actually look forward to every day. Building a plan 1-8 weeks has been great. I like that you can pick up to 5 different types of exercise, chose your daily time commitments, and then on that day modify the time/video for your suggested exercise. I do get frustrated when I do a workout, I can see it on my summary for the day, but it does not “check” off of my plan. I have had this happen 4 times in the last 6 weeks and it is discouraging when I’m on track, but have to redo a workout just to get the completion credit. Competing with other friends has been great. I switched from 8 years with Fitbit Premium to Apple Fitness+ with an Apple Watch primarily because FP got rid of challenges. I would love if I could have 2-3 friends competing with you at a time, but the 1:1 is better than nothing. Sometimes the awards are not totally accurate with the activity that it should be awarding for. There have been times that I have exceeded a previous goal, but the award gets “stuck” at a previous metric. I have used my Apple TV, iPad, and iPhone to exercise and all have maintained a considerably seamless. Overall my Apple Fitness+ experience has exceeded my expectations and previous experience with Fitbit.

Today I spent 2 hours in hard gardening - digging, bending over and weeding, planting, etc - but the app told me I only did a few minutes exercise (grinding coffee!) title: Great for getting a sweat worked up daily in a fun way
body:
I had very low expectations for this app. Most fitness app I’ve looked in to are too in-your-face and aimed at people who want to get buff or whatever. I just wanted something with a more relaxed feel, toned down decor, and fun routines that got me in shape. I have been loving this app for that purpose. 

I’m really impressed with the instructors, and I especially love their diversity in gender, age, body type, etc. One is even currently pregnant, and it’s great to see how she works the modified routines. That, the fact that they use some sign language, and the way one instructor is usually demonstrating a low-impact modified version of the workout makes the classes feel welcoming and accessible no matter how I’m feeling. I think the instructors do a great job at explaining things and being encouraging, sometimes making it clear there’s no “right” way to do it, like the idea is to be moving and enjoying yourself. No one needs to see the mess I make of the dance moves, but I’ve really enjoyed trying them!

The routines have you moving in about the space of a yoga mat, so it works well if you only have a small space in your house to use for workouts. 

I don’t use any of the app’s gamified stuff or awards, so if that’s motivating to you, I’m not sure how this app measures up. For fun at-home routines that work lots of muscles and work up a sweat in 10-20 minutes, I’ve found it to be perfect. Shout out especially to the diverse and kind instructors—if they rotate in more older instructors and more variety in body types, I’d love it even more.

title: Disappointingly Inaccurate & frustrating
body:
UPDATE: 

I’m removing this app for a number of reasons. 1) It doesn’t count steps accurately nor does it recognize every time I go upstairs. 2) The distance it shows is off by at least 15%. 3) I didn’t receive the Awards I earned in December and January. It also looks as if I won’t receive my February Award (which was achieved two days ago). I have screenshots of these issues, but obviously can’t post them.

I recommend that people look for another app to count your steps like I did. I also got another app to keep track of my bike rides. This is quite disappointing. 

I began using this app about five months ago. I must admit I didn’t monitor progress too closely until a couple of months ago. Today I uploaded a pedometer. In a matter of 30 minutes my suspicions were confirmed. Fitness is undercounting or not counting steps. I suspected it when it would count only half of my trips upstairs. Then I realized when it indicated that a two minute brisk walk would close my ring and I would make a circuit of my downstairs, it wouldn’t change the number of steps. If you want a good fitness app, use something else. I have a feeling I’ve been closing my ring every day for the past two months, but this app doesn’t show it.

title: Please ALLOW us to EDIT WORKOUTS
body:
Please. For the love of all things practical. 

Why on earth is it impossible to edit a workout? Life happens and sometimes we forget to start or stop a workout on time. I recently got an award for longest Pilates workout after forgetting to hit ‘end’ on my watch for an hour while caring for my baby immediately after working out. I have countless examples like this which means my data is incorrect and it bothers me to no end. 

Prior to getting an Apple Watch I had a Fitbit and their app is brilliantly easy to navigate for edits: one simply selects a workout from history, then adjusts the times as needed and all corresponding data (steps, heart rate, etc) is then auto populated to match. With Apple Fitness & Health apps I don’t bother looking at workout trends because it’s worthless if it’s incorrect. This is heartbreaking. If I hadn’t made the investment in the watch I would switch back to Fitbit in a heartbeat. 

The variety and quality of workouts, walks, etc offered thru the Fitness app are excellent. If you update the ability to edit workouts in a simple way or if/when I switch back to using a Fitbit and can enjoy the rest of the app without getting hot and bothered then I’ll update my rating.

title: There are better options elsewhere
body: I’m a sucker for gamified exercise, so I thought this would be my jam. But as-is, this app is over-priced and surprisingly under-resourced. There are better gamified exercise programs on video game consoles; I even prefer straight-up online videos to this, as many of the videos have multiple complex moves that are difficult to properly follow on a tiny screen. Most of the instructors have little to say when it comes to proper form, typically encouraging followers to keep up a pace that is unmanageable for newbies to the particular exercise. I appreciated that the exercises were generally, for me, challenging but ultimately don’t find it a good value.

title: Fitness + is Blues Clues for 20-something’s
body: I actively despise Apple Fitness+. It’s cringy LA fakeness at it’s worst. While people blame Peloton for seeming cult-y, nothing can prepare you for this fake energy of the patronizing drivel that’s spoken during each class. It’s as if every instructor (primary + joining friends) has an off-screen boss, forcing artificial smiles and awkward laughs, giggles and reactions at weird moments when nothing funny was said. My class tried really hard to correlate every single moment in the workout to watching a season of your favorite show… it was miserable and repetitive filler-commentary, and all of the music sounded the exact same. The set looks like a fake-brick scene, straight from the musical ‘Rent.’  It’s hard to believe that any one of the instructors has any real experience instructing. How have they not improved things in over a year of producing this content? - so, in short, if you want to watch something with the writing of Blue’s Clues, aimed squarely at super young, insecure 20-something’s that never developed their brains past the 3rd grade, good luck and have at it. As for me, I’m running for the hills!

title: DIFFERENT FITNESS LEVELS NEEDED
body:
Because the app does not offer exercises for differing levels of ability, THE CUSTOMIZED EXERCISE PLANS ARE GARBAGE. They promote quitting and deleting the app. 

The app is truly only useful for people in peak physical shape. Those of us with different fitness abilities are merely an afterthought. This is entirely obvious from the way the so-called modifications receive the briefest of mentions. All of this makes their claims of wanting to promote physical fitness and healthy habits incredibly insulting. 

Instead of treating people with differing levels of fitness as pitiable pariahs, each of the routines should be offered at different experience/ability levels. That would allow for more customization and more engagement. It would also allow for more meaningful tracking of progress. 

For example, I can make it through most of the Core and Yoga routines with no problem. At times I struggle with the Kickboxing routines. And the HIIT, Pilates, and Dance routines are so frustratingly advanced that I rarely make it through an entire exercise. If I could access routines based on my ability and experience for each category, I would actually find the app useful and engaging instead of it making me feel like trash as I struggle through exercises the trainers are doing so breezily. 

With all of the resources at your disposal, Apple, I know you can do better than this.

title: Too much, too little and restricted
body:
The app starts you out very basic, when making my plan I felt restricted, I couldn’t choose how long my workouts would be, what days I would do them or the intensity.

But I had overwhelming choices of trainers. I made a basic plan and got to it.

Day one was fine, I had a core workout and meditation afterwards. In between I opted for a cooldown session. Problem being was there were too few options. I couldn’t find a cooldown that focused on my core, and I really wish I had some warmup stretches before the workout. The meditation was basic, but I couldn’t focus.

The following days the issues became more apparent. No stretches beforehand left me stiff and made the pace of the exercises hard to keep up with, which there are no options for. Day two was also a core exercise, at this point I didn’t know I could switch. 

Day 3 was yet another core exercise! And yes, I maxed out the options for exercises they gave me in my plan, leaving some on the table that I wanted to include. I did learn to switch it out, but again, I couldn’t find a cooldown that went along with the workout.

Overall, this feels like it’s pushing these trainers, who I don’t know, instead of developing a customized plan. Everything feels disjointed. Oh, and I had to delete my plan to change it, because there is NO option to alter it aside from the name. If I cared about my progress I’d have been upset. 

3 days of a 3 month trial was enough to know this isn’t worth my time. I can do better on YouTube.

title: Lots Of Options
body: I’ve exercised for 30 years and have done everything from VHS videos to a gym membership. This app is great. There are multiple exercise categories, such as yoga, kickboxing, strength training, dance, and meditation. You can filter by how long you want to workout (10, 20, 30, or 40 minutes), by trainer, etc. Some of my favorite trainers from other exercise programs are on there, and the trainers who are new to me are also excellent. There are rewards you can get for calories burned, number of days worked out in a week or a month, and so forth but these are not important to me so I can’t comment on them. It is fun to watch my ring progress on screen while I’m working out. There’s also a timer on screen for both the overall workout as well as the individual exercises that helps a lot when you want to try to push through a challenge.

title: Function is subpar
body:
This app is all over the place, so as far as accuracy is concerned- it isn’t. I use a treadmill everyday, I walk consistently all day and yet after 14,000 steps I have not closed my circle today at a measly 230 calories. On the other hand, I had closed the circle after using the treadmill yesterday morning and using the recumbent bike. Why is it so sporadic? 

 Update: 11-12-23 No improvement in this app. Does anyone even support it at all? I am active every day and this app thinks otherwise. For instance today’s routine consisted of the following, starting at 8:00 on a Sunday.

 3 - 20 minute sessions on the recumbent bike at 235 calories per ride. The app only showed “60” calories after 1 hour. 2 (20 minute) - 1 mile sessions on the treadmill and it barely hit 140 after all this. 

1 (20 minute) - 1 mile session late afternoon and it finally closed stating “238”. Honestly, fitness pal is much better in regards to accuracy and consistency.

11-14-23
17,310 steps / 7.1 miles 
Move ring 337/230
It began to seem extremely erratic around September and hasn’t improved since then.

I was averaging around 600 calories on my move ring and earning a different award daily as a result. Now nothing.

title: Paid only version for IPad
body:
Here’s a standing ovation for the modern-day Robin Hoods, except you’re taking from the paying customer and giving to… well, your own coffers. Let’s run through the loot: $1100 for the phone, $650 for the watch, $1500 for the computer, $500 for the headphones, $150 for the Apple TV, and $1300 for the iPad Pro. Now, after emptying our pockets, you’re holding out your hats asking for a $10 monthly if I want to use this pre installed app on my tablet.

It’s fascinating how you’ve turned tech luxury into tech necessity and then have the gall to nickel and dime us for extras. I didn’t realize my tech lineup was an all-you-can-eat buffet for your profit margins. So, tell me when is enough.

title: Great workouts HORRIBLE APP
body:
Let me start by saying I love Apple Fitness trainers, workouts and variety of workouts for all fitness levels... BUT I HATE THIS APP!!!! The moment you open the app youre bombarded with suggestions and new workouts and spotlights which honestly 95% of the time have no interest in at all yet you have to scroll past all of this 3/4 of the way down to get to the trainers. When you get there, the trainers are not in alphabetical order. So for example I love Greg for Strength and Spin and yet hes on the bottom half of the list. Why? When you select a trainer its easy to sort by workout type, length and even music which is great. 

Whats NOT great is if you save or download your workouts they appear at the VERY BOTTOM of the main page in My Library. Why make people scroll to workouts they already chose and want? 

When you get to the saved and downloaded workouts you cant filter either. So if I wanted 20mn workouts or Greg only or Rock only NOPE! You have to scroll through the list to find what you want. Again...why make people scroll so much when the app obviously has the ability to sort?

Can you guys PLEASE make a menu on the first page so I have the option to get to the Trainers or Library (Saved and Downloaded workout)s?

Also cut back the amount of rows of stuff you are pushing. A row or two, cool but 8 or so rows seems a insanely excessive especially when this app doesn't seem to be learning that I obviously would not choose, lets say Rowing, because I don't have a rower not row boat etc! 

Also maybe allow people to set a row of stuff to keep an eye on. Like alert me for new Greg workouts.

title: Loved it until the update
body:
I have been using the Fitness+ App since January 2023. I fell in love with it during my free trial and paid for the year subscription with no regrets. I have been using it religiously since then and have been praising it up and down to everyone I know. 

Until the update. 

The iOS 17 update came with a few amazing perks like the stacks and the customizable plans which I thought were amazing because I could finally set up my own routine and not have to think about which workouts to do each morning. The most recent plan I set up included: Pilates, Strength, Core, HIIT and Mindful Cooldowns. I had it all neatly set up:

MWF: 30min Strength, 5min Core, 10min Cooldown

TuTh: 10min HIIT, 30min Pilates, 5min Cooldown

Two weeks flew by and I had not missed a day. I loved that I could swap the workouts for more or less time if I needed and everything was working! Until yesterday (Wed), I decided to swap my 5 minute core for a 20 minute one and for some reason the whole thing glitched. After I completed the workout it said “You still have time to complete your workouts today!” But I just did? And then when I looked to the next day to see what was on deck instead of it saying Pilates, HIIT and Cooldown, it had ALL three listed as Mindful Cooldowns (the same exact 5 minute video with Molly to be exact). It was the same for Friday but it had all three workouts listed as 5minute Core with Betina (the same one). I even got a notification this morning that said “you have three Mindful Cooldowns today!” What? No I don’t!

Ugh so frustrating. I excused it as an unfortunate glitch and deleted the plan. But then when I opened the app up again there it was, the plan was back up on deck and notifying me that I had a workout to do. Excuse me? Didn’t I delete this plan? 

I get that all updates will come with glitches so I haven’t given up on Fitness+ yet, but I hope these get fixed because as someone who deals with anxiety and likes a structure routine, this really threw me off and I’m a bit disappointed. Please fix the glitches! I still want to live this app (especially since I’m paying for it!)

title: “Stand” and “Flights Climbed” Inaccurate/Makes Me Neurotic
body: I’ve been using this app via my Apple Watch since probably 2015 (it’s now 2023).  I do lots of different kinds of exercise and am very self motivated, so I didn’t NEED to use this app, but I like comparing data, so I was interested in seeing what it said about my various fitness indicators.  Overall, there are a lot of helpful components to this app.  Unfortunately, there are enough inaccuracies and non-customizable features that it is sometimes infuriating.  The “stand” ring is one of those.  I can’t tell you how many times I have stood for 50 minutes straight only to have it tell me that”it’s time to stand!”  If the watch is unable to accurately perceive standing, or if Apple is actually trying to encourage lower body movement (not just standing), then, please, rename the rings Movement (instead of Standing), Exercise, and Calories (instead of Movement).  The Flights Climbed feature also doesn’t work.  I could walk up and down the steps in my house for thirty minutes straight and have not a single flight of steps be logged.  I also take issue with the watch setting goals for me (I’m thinking of the monthly goals here).  Yes, I aim to be fit, but sometimes I have other priorities than burning a certain number of movement calories in a month.  And what if I’m on a plan all day?  Perhaps standing every hour is not one of my goals that day.  Let me be in charge of my goals.  On the other hand, sometimes I spend all day hiking… and my watch runs out of battery life during the hike.  So my calories and exercise can’t even be recorded.  I don’t like having these inaccuracies recorded as fact.    And I don’t like how this watch is encouraging me to be neurotic about something that “matters,” but that I shouldn’t be obsessive about.  I shouldn’t feel like I need to shake my arm up and down at the end of the day to push the Movement ring across the finish line and appease an APP.  In the end, this “health” app is negatively affecting my mental health.

title: Really Lacking Features
body:
It’s a good set it and forget it app. I’m not interested in Fitness+ because it seems to be focused on workout videos, and I have no issues planning my own workouts.

What I do struggle with is a lack of basic features between the app and the watch. First, you only have the ability to customize the workouts on your watch. Look I’m getting older and my eyes don’t want to stare at the tiny screen and try to adjust the intervals, time for each rep, goals, etc., Also, the only notification that the work intervals has ended and recovery interval has started is the watch vibrates. It’s a very subtle vibrate so if you’re running and the watch isn’t super tight, it’s easy to miss. Especially if you’re wearing layers. There should be options for a sound to go with it (the alert option is only to notify you of target metrics.) if you want to charge for more customization go for it but I prefer the Under Armor Map My Run app for my running training because it’s a lot more flexible, and is a reasonable rate for what you get.

Last thing, I’d love to know the algorithm for these monthly challenges. October told me how I was doing so well with open water swim and to get three this month.  1. I have never done an open water swim as I only do laps in a pool, and 2. I live in Michigan. Now maybe some brave souls may hit the lake in October but not me. Not sure what the app is looking to motivate me to do here but it might want to take into account location when making certain recommendations or challenge goals.
