title: Seriously lacks “workout” class for natural pedestrian travel
body: This app, and the associated “workout” app for Apple Watch, conspicuously lacks an object class to accurately reflect the health implications of natural daily traversals across short to medium distances, or which account for various essential variables such as load weight and atmospheric conditions. The dev teams on these projects are clearly intelligent enough to recognize these glaring confounds, but statistics are still presented within native interfaces as though they have already been reliably verified. No information is better than false information! [lowered rating to 2 stars due to unresponsiveness and possibly deliberate obfuscation of my comments by Apple or the dev team(s)]

title: Love this App, but Not Enough for Seniors
body:
This is a great app, especially the watch integration… but Fitness+ workouts are very limited for seniors & others with mobility limitations. Although they include modifications in most of the workouts, far too many involve getting on and off the floor. They have one set of very nice “Workouts for Older Adults” but after 2 years they’re getting old. And even one of those requires getting on the floor so I mostly skip it. While many of us can do it if necessary, it can take us long enough that we’ve missed a lot of the workout in the process. At a minimum, if they don’t want to make more senior-specific workouts, AT LEAST enable us to search for workouts that don’t involve being on the floor. Nothing more frustrating that starting a workout that looks promising only to find out they’ve buried some floor exercises in the middle. Half the old ladies in my water aerobics classes wear Apple Watches, but I won’t recommend Fitness+ until there is a better library of workouts for us as virtually all of us feel the same way about getting on the floor. 
Hope someone actually pays attention to these reviews & works on this!

title: Fitness Competitions
body:
Every week, my Wife and I use the Fitness app to challenge each other. I have a few questions about some of the functionality. 

1. Why is there a 12-hour break between ending a workout and being able to rematch? Better yet, why not allow longer workout competitions or auto rematch? 

2. When each competition ends, I have to look all over the app, like Indiana Jones, to find the competition stats and ending scores. Why must search and rescue be activated just to see how much my Wife kicked my butt. 

3. The sleep stats, which is the most important of all. Why are the sensors and stats so lame? If Fitbit can figure this out, I’m certain Apple can do it. The lack of focus on this issue is a bit disappointing when it’s a medical fact good sleep and good health go hand in hand.

title: Great
body:
I think this is great. For the cost, you get a lot of great content. 
My only suggestion would be to incorporate better planning for a workout plan. Every workout is “all out” and it would be nice to see a recovery workout option mixed in. Also if you are doing strength multiple days in a row they don’t take into account upper and lower body. You might have 2 or 3 lower body workouts in a row. You can switch them up, but it would be nice to see.  
Other than that I think this is as good as it gets. The workouts are all tailored for you to do at home with the equipment you have. I have done every type of workout available and the trainers and music are all great. The complaints I see confuse me because if you have tried anything else, nothing even come close to what you get here. Especially for the price. 
Great job!

title: Great instructors & content, needs better playback functionality
body:
Pros:
+ inspiring, motivating, inclusive instructors
+ nice variety of workout options
+ good range of timing and intensity options

Cons:
- can’t control playback at all, meaning you can’t scrub backwards if you miss an instruction or move. You either have to start all over or stay uneven the whole time - not ideal!
- can’t create a queue or playlists for workouts if you want to stack a few together for a longer session; you have to go back into your saved and scroll allllll the way through to find what you want
author: songbird528

title: It took 5 minutes of a 3 month free trial to decide this app is garbage
body:
It took 5 minutes of a 3 month free trial to decide this app is garbage.  I’m just trying to use this app on Apple TV but they require a second apple device (iPhone or iWatch), just to use this on Apple TV.  For every workout on AppleTV, you have to unlock your iPhone.  But then you have to unlock your iPhone every 4 minutes or the workout on AppleTV stops streaming.  How stupid is that?  I’m trying to workout, quit making me unlock my iPhone every 4 minutes.

You can’t fast forward through workouts to sample one before doing it.  You have to do watch nearly the entire workout to decide if that’s one you even want to start.  Get Beachbody on Demand instead, it has a better workout catalog, a better user interface, less boring workouts, and you can use it on any device of your choosing without having to link two devices together and keep unlocking the second device every four minutes.

title: I don’t get the hate, this app is great!
body:
First of all, I’m not a bot and I wasn’t paid to write this. I used the app for the first time today and did a 30 minute run. Running has always been hard for me because I find it difficult to get out of my head and it seems like it just drags on and on. I’m lucky if I make it a mile and a half when I, first getting back into it, and at my best I only ever made it up to 4 miles. 

Today, however, I did the 30 minute run with Scott and I was really surprised. They way they “gamify” the run if you have an Apple Watch where you can see you heart rate, distance, cadence, and activity ring was cool, but the “Burn Bar” was the coolest feature. This is Apples definition of what it is: 

“ The Burn Bar is a way for you to compare your effort to others who've done the same workout. It adjusts to account for weight to allow for an equal comparison and is shown as your calories burned. If you leave it on, your workout data is anonymously added to the Burn Bar competition. The Burn Bar is available for High Intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Treadmill, Cycling, and Rowing workouts.”

I’m a little competitive by nature, so having this really pushed me to work harder, and the combination of the interesting commentary from Scott and everything I mentioned above contributed to me running 2.4 miles on day one (and I am out of shape). I’d encourage you to give this a try, especially if you have an Apple Watch.

title: A bit thoughtless
body:
I’ve never used the fitness app for my iPhone for as long as I’ve had one. The latest iPhone update automatically set it up for me with no input, warning or instruction from me. While I understand the desire for technology to be useful and engaging with little input, it wasn’t helpful for me. I am in recovery from severe eating disorders for 2 years now, and randomly getting daily notifications of how many calories I needed to burn today was very unnecessary. When you’re someone who used to count every calorie in every food and physical action for years, it’s not just numbers to ‘close a ring’. It’s temptation to slip back into eating 800-1000 calories a day while tracking workouts to burn 300-500. 

As a result, I have little interest in using the product. Please be more conscientious about how automatic setup could not be received well. If a tutorial asking to set up had been the first few notifications rather than a number telling me to move to burn more calories, it wouldn’t have been so jarring.

title: Fitness + pros and cons
body: I used Fiton in the past but my husband encouraged me to try Fitness+ since I now have a watch that supports it. I love the integration between my Apple TV and watch! So cool to see my activity on the top of the screen. There seems to be lots of great exercises offered, taught by great teachers. I also love that you can see the music tracks from any workout in case you like a song and want to add it to your library. Great feature! What could use some work, in my opinion, is the filtering and menus. I absolutely hate scrolling down to the bottom to get to my saved workouts. I also hate not being able to have menus instead of through the whole page to find something. This is for both the mobile and Apple TV versions. And I was so used to being able to filter workouts based on fitness level that now it seems so clunky and cumbersome to have to watch a preview to see what I might encounter and try to gauge the level from there. When you have 30 minutes in the morning, the last thing you want to do is scroll though a bunch of workouts you’d never consider just to get to something that seems doable. I love yoga workouts so maybe there could be a way to quickly access yoga workout and then filter by level and time from there. Because let’s be real, even with modifications, not every yoga workout can be for beginners. And beginner ones aren’t ideal for expert level. This seems like such a no brainer, to have better filters, I’m honestly surprised Apple let it go out and stay like this.

For the last month, I’ve closed my ring nearly every single day, but I’ve been realizing lately my “awards” are NOT reflecting that. This was a huge motivator for me to continue to use this app. There’s really no purpose otherwise, there are plenty of fitness apps out here I could use otherwise. I enjoy setting a goal, reaching it, and being rewarded for so. I have completed a full week, Monday-Sunday, and yet the award has not be “awarded”, along with my longest streak, being at 8+ days. Also, BIG CON for me is the week running Monday-Sunday, and calendar reflecting that as well. Like really, where in the world is that normal? Everything is Sunday-Saturday, and as for myself completing goals, that is the way my brain is thinking. Being different in this way is just an annoyance, along with the fact it’s not an option that can be changed. Honestly, if my “awards” are not at least fixed, I’m over and done with this app. The issues are too much to continue.

title: Now I’m Unhappy…
body:
Updated again on 7/2/23

 Yesterday I mentioned that the ‘longest move streak’ was messed up again and not calculating correctly (see the bottom of the original review) as is the problem with all the counters in this app along with all the calculated fitness and cardiac formulas that use the data from those counters. Today, I see that although I have exceeded my goal once more, I have suddenly lost the 169 days in the ‘longest move streak’ counter which was what was in that counter yesterday.. it now informs me that I have a “streak” of 35 days.. oh how wonderful! Note that the number 35 pops up repeatedly in counters when the programming code goes awry. If this apple watch appropriate app is not going to function and there are very few other fitness apps available to connect to apple watch, it’s time to dump apple products for me.. it’s too bad since I really wanted their products to be better than others in the current market. I wish users of this product luck and hope the offerings expand or at least live up to minimum expectations..

Original review 5/2023:
Okay, who messed up the code in the last update? How does this happen..? After installing the most recent update, I now have previously functional features no longer working. I was 123 days in on a Longest Streak goal on 5/19, but on 5/20, that Longest Streak was reset to 35 days in length.. why? How can this be corrected? That’s one more problem in an app that has several major areas that needs to be addressed. The biggest issue is one previously mentioned by other reviewers and that is the tracking of all daily movement and its effect on active and inactive calorie burn levels. To get even close to accurate data, the workout feature has to be engaged for any and every activity period one engages in.. including normal daily chores like cooking, playing with the dog, doing the laundry, etc. otherwise you get little to no addition to your calories burned count. Oh, but if you accidentally leave your workout engaged overnight? Wow! I’ve burned nearly 4,000 calories while sleeping!! Got an Award for it, too!! Developers please note, those kind of errors added to the list of issues others have pointed out make this app virtually useless. 
Update: 7/1/23 Well for a short time after I wrote the original review, it appeared that at least one of the rolling counters.. longest move streak.. had been corrected, but I was wrong in assuming it was now functioning correctly. Today I discovered that if you go to a prior month to check something on a particular day and that day also had a ‘longest move streak’ count on it and you jump back out of the app without returning to today and today’s move stats, you end up with today’s stats suddenly changing. My longest move streak was 169 this morning, yet after I checked stats on an exercise program I had designed and used on 3 days last month, my ‘streak’ became 166!! What the heck are you doing here? Yes, I’m looking at one item, but it’s the same with all your “counter stats”.. any time you are using this app, the only thing you can be certain of is that every single counter will be inaccurate. The problem is compounded as those individual stats are used to determine others.. like Vox and cardiac variability.. that makes not just the one item inaccurate, it also makes every other aspect useless. Your steps, stairs, overall activity calorie burn, et al. are all inaccurate and if the designers are unwilling to take a look at the entire app and do some serious analysis and reprogramming to make it function correctly, why bother to download it?

title: Excellent for fitness rebooters - but the UI/UX needs help
body:
My wife signed up for this so with the Family Plan I was able to try it out. I have been struggling for years (pandemic didn't help!) to recover from what I like to call "office work syndrome" where I had let my level of fitness drop to sedentary. I have on the hunt to find a program that would provide me with the full range of exercises from absolute beginner to as far as I could take my new self. 

I really like that even with the "XXX for Beginners" series, there is a range of abilities represented so I can get stronger without hurting myself (a recurring issue on my journey). The people they have chosen are very good at expressing and projecting support and encouragement while also challenging us to stretch ourselves - so unlike the verbal abuse I experienced in high school football!

The only reason for 4 and not 5 stars is that I would just love (1) to have my Library accessible at the top when I open the app up rather than having to scroll down to the bottom - it took me several times of roaming around the app to figure that out 🤯😱😤; (2) as a complement to my first ask, for Pete's sake add Search functionality🥺 (It seems like it SEARCH would have been part of the Alpha version 🤨 but if it was, someone in Product decided that was not cool or whatever "the kids" are saying these days); and (3) add the ability to suggest a workout with someone else by sharing it the same way I can share almost anything else - this is different from the share functionality that is built in, let's all work out together regardless of where we are in the world. 

These three issues are not deal-breakers but they seem to be mostly UI/UX issues that could be implemented without having to refactor code (can you tell I've worked in software 😜). Thanks for listening.

title: Great Coaches, Music, and Vibe, But Technique is Missing
body: The Fitness+ app by Apple offers a fantastic workout experience with motivating coaches and energizing music. The app provides a wide range of workouts, catering to different fitness levels and preferences. However, one major drawback is the lack of detailed exercise technique guidance. This becomes particularly noticeable during fast-paced HIIT workouts, where new movements are introduced quickly. Currently, exercises are only shown from a frontal view, without close-ups or slow-motion demonstrations. This absence of technique guidance hinders users' ability to perform exercises correctly and increases the risk of injury. To address this issue, the app should include separate short videos that focus on the techniques of the exercises, allowing users to familiarize themselves with proper form before starting the workout

title: Better Search Features Please!
body:
Fitness+ was pointed out to me last week, and I decided to give it a try. My gym has been unable to offer yoga classes lately, and I've been wanting to get back into a daily flow. 
The videos are easy to follow, but I’m also not a new yogi. Most of the time I know what a coach is talking about without having to see the screen. There's a wide range of workouts, and the integration with my watch is far more seamless than other fitness Apps I've used. 
However, there is one thing I feel could use improvement: search functions and filters. There is no search bar, and the only filters available for activities are trainer, time, music style, and equipment if necessary. Titles for workouts are non-descriptive. So the only way to know what specifically is going on in a class, and if it's what you are looking for is to open its description. I don't care what style of music we're working with, I want to know if this is a fast-paced Vinyasina that will have me sweating buckets or a quiet yin flow that digs deep into my hip flexors. Are we focusing on balance, strength, twists, or range of motion? I have to add an extra 5-10 minutes onto my practice just to go through the library to find what I am looking for in a flow that day. Being able to filter results by preferences like “deep stretch” or “shoulders” would be so useful. Or even both! 
I want to like Fitness+ more, but Im on the fence about it considering it's easier to find a video class with a listed focus on YouTube.

title: Very INACCURATE

Why would I pay for upgrades on something when it can’t get the basics correct?

title: Enhancements needed
body:
Overall the Fitness app functions well and effectively monitors activities. Some enhancements that would make this a 4-5 star app in my opinion:
 1. Indoor walk and run activities - treadmill users should have the ability to add elevation and mileage to the work outs as this would more accurately reflect the distance and intensity of the workout. (Other apps allow you to do this but we should not need other apps). 
 2. Cycling (indoor or outdoor) - app should convert strides or measured rpms to steps for the purposes of accurately capturing steps for the day. On days I ride rather than walk / run the app tells me I am taking less steps because it doesn’t factor in cycling. Example - I am a Peleton Bike user - I do certain workouts that cover between 10-20 miles on the bike (mostly in winter when temperatures make running less optimal) and I get negative trend results because I am meeting my rings through other means. 
 3. App should ask some basic demographic information so that the “challenges” are appropriate. Certain of the challenges proposed do not consider whether or not a person works full time. I recently received a challenge that suggested I average 150 active minutes a day for a month. Addressing these would greatly enhance the app.

title: Inadequate
body: Pretty graphics. Still vaporware.  Inaccurate. Misleading. Not worth the trouble.  I’m a senior and walk my dog 2-4 miles daily at a normal 3 mile/hr pace or 490 meters/minute which is in the above average heart health range for my age. We occasionally stop to say hello to neighbors or to pick up any poos. This app translates my stops into slower less healthy categories, even if I attempt the hard to use ‘pause’ feature. I’m in better than average shape for my age.  But it averages my not using the app into it’s report on as if I’m  not exercising reducing scores in it’s vO2 estimates.  Using the exercise function is probably not worth the hassle although I would like a way to better integrate my walks and other exercise into the Apple Health app. Oh well.
author: Sportsfan2

title: More intuitive, less insults
body: I am an active individual, I work out 5-6 times a week. I have a dress watch and an Apple Watch so I don’t exclusively wear my Apple Watch everyday but rather for certain activities and for when I want to leverage apps such as Strava. The issues I have with this app are as follows: 1. It doesn’t recognize when I haven’t worn my Apple Watch or only worn it for a specific activity. So on putting on my Apple Watch in the morning the first message I might receive is “You took it easy yesterday”. I find this incredibly insulting. This could easily say welcome back or something more motivating and positive. 2. The exercise tracker itself is poor. I could do 100 burpees and it would barely count as exercise yet a “brisk” walk does register. Hopefully these can be improved as I like the simplicity of closing rings. Until then I will do without the insults.

A couple of small things would make it better. For the treadmill workouts they need an additional filter to find hills vs speed workouts so you don’t have to read each description before finding what you want. I would also move the MyLibrary from the bottom of the app to closer to the top, so I don’t have to scroll by everything to get to my favorites. body:

1. Add more knee friendly workouts. Lots of the HIIT workouts involve a lot of jumping. There are lots of great HIIT workouts that are knee friendly. 

2. Speaking of knee friendly workouts maybe you could have MrandMrs Muscle as guest trainers. They offer lots of high energy HIIT workouts as well as knee friendly ones. 

3. It would be great if there could be different music. I like all the variety but maybe adding some disco, funk, upbeat R & B and even some 70’s or 80’s playlist would add a bit more variety.

body:
I think this is a really cool app, and I honestly think it’s a good deal to. However, it’s outdated in certain ways that I don’t have to mention because others already have, but one of the main ways that it’s outdated is it doesn’t give you the option to turn off the calorie counter, it doesn’t give you the option to turn off the calorie goal setting. Considering the culture of eating disorders, you would think that apple would be more sensitive and make an option for people to turn it off. I am very athletic, but I could care less about calories. I could care less about counting them. Personally, I wish I could turn the option off. I know for a fact that others would be very triggered by the calorie counting setting on this app. I know many people who do not use it because they can’t turn it off. Get with the times Apple! 

Also, why isn’t there an option to favorite work outs? I would like to have a folder available for me to go back to workouts or audio tracks I’d like to do or revisit. 

I truly hope somebody at Apple reads this and addresses these issues. 

Oh … the home page is also way to complicated. Needs to be easier to navigate ! 

We’ll see if I stay with this app or not.

title: Mostly great, needs some updates and fixes
body:
Update: Apple has addressed many of the issues in my original review. Thank you! My new suggestions are: let us schedule rest days or input sick days on our watch. Sometimes I get discouraged by breaking a streak even when doing so is needed or beyond my body’s control. Rest days let me manage my time without getting fixated; and they’re necessary when sick. Being able to schedule rest days so I took them before I got injured or burnt out would make it easier to stay on track and avoid feeling discouraged about progress. I’ve got a packed, demanding life. I’ve got school age kids who make our home a revolving door of viruses. I’m in my 40’s and more prone to injury than I was in my 20’s. I feel like the metrics could make room for all of that. 

The trainer team is phenomenal. 5 stars to the trainers and whoever was in charge of casting them. The workouts and variety of workouts are also great. Items I would like to see addressed and updated: 1) [had been fixed] 2) [has been fixed. Thank you!]. 3) [addressed but not per my suggestions for audio. Still sounds better overall]. 4) where I am connected to friends on my fitness/watch; I find a lot of the automatic responses pretty rude and sarcastic. I’m all in favor of less smack talk and more positive affirmation/encouragement. I would be mortified if I accidentally sent one of my tender hearted friends one of those mean responses.

iPhone

title: Two Reasons I’ll Probably Cancel
body:
1. There’s no Apple Fitness+ app available on Fire TV. I don’t understand this — there’s an Apple TV app, so it’s not like a brand thing. In any event, if I’m paying a month fee for a fitness app, I’d like to be able to access it on my TV, without having to use screen sharing which rarely works well enough to use for a class. 

2. There’s no way to turn the music volume up and instructor voice down. I mainly use the app for spinning classes. I use subtitles on all my apps/TV. I’d really like the option to turn up the music without turning up the instructor’s voice. Especially when I pick a class based on music. 

For these reasons, it’s hard to justify a $10/mo fee.

I wish “My Library” had more organizational features— more similar to the search function. It would be nice if the completed workouts were separate from the just added workouts. title: With the watch it’s getting better.
body:
3/7/23 Since posting the first review I’ve gotten an Apple Watch. As mentioned before I never knew how/when the “steps” were updated but another really frustrating thing were my days off work I never met my goals on my days off. Everyone tends to have lazy days here and there but I knew I was doing things, now that I have the watch I meet my goals *almost* everyday and I’ve increased my goals every week for the last 3 weeks. 

** Three things that would make a great difference at least for me would be-
1. On the watch app let it be a choice what is shown currently the three screens are the rings currently, sharing your progress and your awards. I couldn’t care less about sharing and my awards I can see much better on my phone. 
2. Why do I have to wait for the app to recognize that I’m going for a walk? Why can’t I tell the app that I’m about to go for a walk/run?
3. Since most people work in different spaces than how they spend their time off can we get 2-3 “weekend” days? I’d be more inclined to get outside and do something if I knew I could still meet a goal even if it isn’t the high number I meet daily at my job (it’s a warehouse where I walk a lot) 

10/23/22 It’s definitely motivating to get moving but it’s equally frustrating bc I don’t know how/when it updates. It definitely isn’t live stream tracking as you go, but it seems like maybe after you’ve stopped moving for a few minutes that’s when it catches up? Idk. I wouldn’t mind the delay if I could just know what that delay is, for one I would just keep moving instead of constantly looking at my rings and 2 my battery would appreciate not dying as fast. Does this app work with the Fitbit smart watch?

title: Wonderful App - Just a Few Requests
body:
In late December last year, I got my first Apple watch. I’m in my late 20s and was previously an android user and had a Garmin smartwatch. With the new watch, I’ve been using the Fitness+ content as part of the free trial semi-regularly (at least twice a week). I have never been an athlete or had much experience in the gym, and I really enjoy these guided workouts.

The Good
-Great variety and number of workouts
-Diverse trainers
-New content with variety of music
-Multiple different types of guided workouts and meditations
-Real Time updates from watch when using Apple screen (iPad or phone, does show when AirPlaying to a non-Apple device)
-Modifications available (walk or run, modifications shown by other trainers)

The (Slightly) Bad
-While you can filter on certain aspects like time, music, and trainer, you can’t search for keywords. I’d love to be able to search for “Taylor Swift” or a certain theme and find workouts related to that.
-My Library and saving isn’t that easy to navigate. When I save a workout to my library, I have to scroll all the way down to view it on the phone app. I would love to see folders you can name yourself so I can organize saved workouts, as well as a quicker navigation to this. 
-Collections are a cool idea, but I always have to navigate back to them. I wish there was a way to save all workouts in a collection to my library, or save a collection so that I can quickly return to it. Something like a progress bar would be really cool here as well. Seeing something like “You’re 40% through the ____ collection!” would be awesome.

All in all I think it is a well designed and useful fitness app! I will be renewing my subscription, but I look forward to any improvements they make.

The welcoming mood and contagious positivity that Fitness + trainers bring to every session adds to inclusion. Each coach in their own individual way sends the message that we all belong in the world and are strong enough to rise to our challenges. As a survivor of early childhood PTSD, exercise has always been an important therapy (reclaiming control of my body). Fitness + adds something I can’t exactly describe - as though each session heals me in spirit as well as body. THANK YOU SO MUCH for this essential new level in my healing.

The app is very easy to use and has major potential to earn a 5 star rating but the layout of the Fitness+ portion needs improvement so I’ve deducted a star from my review for ease of use. My library is all the way at the bottom of the app when it should be at the top underneath the New This Week video. If you decide to do one of their Collections there’s no way to pin it or add it to your library so you’ll have to scroll down and swipe through the collections each and every time you want to do a workout within the collection you picked.

I also deducted a star because the app doesn’t really work on Apple TV that well so I end up just having to cast it from my phone which is annoying as well.

title: Bad tracking
body:
- The Stand tracking is essentially useless. I do not stand 1 minute every hour but it gives credit somehow for moving at other times and/or just sitting. Yet other times I’ll be moving for hours and still be low on Standing. Just a useless implementation.

- The heart rate accuracy is like every other wrist based monitor: poor accuracy - sometimes nothing shown, sometimes off by 10bpm; inability to catch intervals. Also to save the battery the watch does not track heart rate every second like say a Garmin.

- The ipad fitness app looks to be workouts only and not an interface like the watch

- If you do yard work or have a manual labor job your calories are vastly underreported. I believe it’s due to the poor heart rate measurements. Who knows, it’s ineffective.

I don’t love Garnin watches (you still need a chest strap for accurate heart rates while exercising) but they’re better fitness watches by far compared to an apple watch and this half baked app.
author: POOBAHHHH

title: Like vids buuuut
body: Really enjoy quality of vids and instructors. HOWEVER the app needs work in terms of functionality. I workout with my friend and use SharePlay / share screen. The huge downside is after each vid we have to literally hang up and call again in order to play next vid. Meaning if we began with mediation and now want to move on to hiit we have to exit out of the app and the call. Then I have to call him again, SharePlay / sharescreen , he has to accept and then we can workout. This has to be done for EACH workout/vid. No matter if I SharePlay from inside the fitness app or share screen from FaceTime. Trust me we troubleshooted this until we couldn’t anymore lol. PLEASE FIX THIS BUG not only is it annoying to have to do that for each vid it interrupts the flow of our workouts. We should be able to workout to as many vids as we want once we’re sharing the screen. We both have the app so it’s no pirating going on. For example we workout to three/four vids a day. It’s seems like it’s a bug tho and not a limitation because when I end the first workout it still says it’s connected to my friend yet my friend is not connected on his side. If I go to the next video it says it’s still sharing with him but it’s not. So we have to exit and come back in. Both our phones are updated so it’s not that. Second bug is if you’re the one shareplaying you cannot use earbuds or headphones or Bluetooth speaker. If you’re the partner NOT sharing your screen you CAN use them. Both of us should be able to use earbuds headphones or a speaker. I know this because I could not use any of my devices once I added them it would not play volume in my ear and he could no longer hear me. But he had his earbuds in and I could hear him and he could hear the vid. I then closed out of SharePlay and ended call and had him initiate the SharePlay and call when we did that I was able to utilize all three devices but he could not. please fix or upgrade that feature so we’re both able to utilize any of those devices The first bug is the most important because it deals with the flow of the workout. These next features I would upgrade on next update: 1. Adding the ability to google cast and airplay. I know you’re an apple product but as you know most tvs are not so both are absolutely needed. We need to be able to share this w/tv screen to make larger. And/Or make a desktop or online version we can login into so at least it’s on the computer sized screen. 2. Adding mobility vids similar to Tracey Anderson technique where you are constantly moving within a pose or exercise. Mobility is so important for the body as we age. 3. Add a TRUE yoga for beginners vid. I’m very familiar with yoga but my partner is not. Beginners need a vid series that goes through each pose. The teachings. So that they can then do the beginner vids you already have and then move into the others. But the Basics are needed first and that’s what it can be called. Basics of yoga

title: No where near what it should be
body:
This does not hold a candle to Garmin connect.  There is no way to edit data of a completed workout.  Example, you do an indoor track run so you select outdoor run because the indoor run assumes treadmill. (And it’s suggested in the apple forums to select outdoor run for indoor track runs) The gps data is all jacked up and gives inaccurate distance. Now your vo2max is all screwed up.  You’d think you’d be able to just go into the workout and change the distance.  Nope. Can’t do it. You can only delete it.  
There is no suggested recovery.  There is no workload.  You can’t create your own workout like a run and lift. You have to add a new workout. What I mean is, there isn’t a way to set up a single workout that has two different types of workouts in it.  Like I run, pause, then lift weights.  You have to select run, then add a new workout and select lifting.   
The starting and stopping or pausing of workouts isn’t the best.  If you select any run, you better be prepared to run in the next 3 seconds. You can’t just hit a side button and start the run run that way.   On my ultra, hitting the action button only starts the last type of workout. So if I hit that, I better be doing whatever the last workout is.  Which I won’t be because I run then lift, again, two different types of workout. 
I wanted to like this watch and fitness app. But it just isn’t anywhere near what Garmin does.

There are no fast forward or rewind controls, so if you miss an instruction, get interrupted by the kids, or the app glitches, there is no way to get back to where you were in your workout. It seems like apple wants the app to feel like an actual workout class, where you do whatever workout is scheduled for the day and once you start you go until the end, but their stubbornness with philosophy and feel kills usability. Especially fast forward and rewind is such a basic feature that the only explanation is they are intentionally leaving it out. I have really enjoyed the workouts, but will cancel my subscription after the trial because of the app.

Recently, I developed arthritis in my hands and find many of the Yoga and Palates workouts very hand-intensive.  It would be good if the descriptions could be enhanced to provide the info needed to select a workout with minimum impact on hands and wrists.  Molly’s Yoga workout #110 is a great example of a workout with minimum impact on wrists, but it is nowhere in the description although the preview does mention it. Other people have issues with knees, shoulders, etc.  So more detailed info in the descriptions would be a huge benefit to many.
Also, all the workouts show options for those not in top condition, however, the camera does not spend enough time on those demonstrations to be effective.

title: Triggering for ED/ED recovery
body: This app was added automatically to my iPhone, with onboarding that makes the user set a caloric goal for low, medium, or high. This is triggering for people with ED histories, especially ones that involve calorie counting and excessive exercise. Just because setting a caloric goal might be standard practice for certain fitness apps doesn’t mean that is actually a positive or healthy practice! Apple automatically adding this app—without regard for how doing so might negatively affect vulnerable populations’ health and well-being, let alone contribute to harmful ideas about health and weight overall—was upsetting and disappointing.

It would also be cool if you could do a really big workout series for under 13, and it would also be cool ifyou added a more advanced filtering system option, such as workouts with no jumping for apartment situations. I was reading a lot of negative reviews and I realized many of them have ideas and suggestions that usually phrased aggressively but are actually good ideas. A lot of the best apps have responses to a lot of reviews so consider reading those. 

The Fitness+ subscription seemed a little pricey at first but it has been so benificial and with all the hard work those trainers put in to bring those workouts to the app it seems like a really fair price. This is overall an amazing app and so easy to use. It does seem like the accuracy of the rings could use some work though.

title: Poor layout & Excessive Pointless Info
body:
So as a runner, I was very excited to get my Apple Watch. I could finally track my running distance, as well as my avg running speed, and not worry about a phone in my pocket. All I’m asking for out of this app, is for it to actively  and accurately track my running speed in mph. Yet, whenever you go into this app, all u keep getting thrown at you, are these exceedingly useless facts about your heart rate, the distance you’ve ran, and the amount of time you ran it in. Listen Apple, I know it’s hard since Jobs ain’t there anymore, but you have missed your target on this one WAY wide left. You are missing the beautiful simplicity that was Apple in times past. GIVE ME THE BASIC FACTS. LAY THEM OUT PLAINLY. Idiot-proof in this case, also means genius-approved. 
STOP overthinking this. 
NONE of us care about the minutia this app is spewing out as dumb factoids, hoping you use them to improve your health. 
Give the people what they want. 
Steve Jobs understood that. 
Apple USED to represent that.

title: Need more senior content
body:
I have just received an Apple Watch for Christmas. I was very excited about the fitness part of the experience and the safety for me if I should fall or have a car crash. 
Problem is you have very little content geared to seniors and the issues they face when trying to do certain exercises. I had a total knee replacement this year and can’t kneel. There are no routines in any of the workouts I looked at that take this into account. I would also like to see stretching exercises and strength training with bands. 
Please make seniors more of a priority when putting these workouts together! Put the workouts in a special section so they are easy to find  This is surely an area that you need to address since millions of seniors have the same issues and are buying your watch for the same reasons. 
I am on my 3 month trial. I need more content to make this worthwhile. Otherwise I can just watch some very good workouts on YouTube for free and log them in myself.

title: No Roku compatibility
body:
In all the years since the Fitness app and related classes, especially in light of the Apple bundle (for which I pay), it is wholly ridiculous that there is STILL NO Roku compatibility. I am supposed to hold my iPhone while watching a class???? How is that convenient? I am 52, and a man was put on the moon before I was born, but Apple can’t create a way to make this possible 🙄
So, sadly I pay for Fitness in my Apple bundle and I never do one class because despite my Apple TV app on my Roku TV, there’s no way to see Fitness because Apple can’t put it there 🤷‍♀️ 
Fitness is therefore unusable to me. 
I have tried casting through Airplay, but every time my husband and I attempt the process we are left to go around in circles. We begin the setup, but we need to enter a code that we don’t have. We have looked up the Roku TV model #, and it is correct. This just never works. 
Look, the end all is that we can’t be the only ones with this experience and Apple just never makes this a possibility. I do not know why. I keep checking on this every once in awhile to see that if enough time passes, Fitness will be added to the AppleTV app on Roku. I hold out hope. It’s almost the end of 2022. Who knows? Maybe 2023’s the year.

title: Too many issues
body:
I like the variety of workouts and the workouts themselves, but wish Apple could work out the following issues:
- It would be great if you could pause and then resume a workout after being interrupted. I’ve tried several times to resume a workout after pausing; each time that I’ve tried doing so, the audio works but there is no video. 
-Along those same lines, there should be a way to rewind or fast forward a workout. From what I can tell, there is not.
- Workouts are listed by most recent. There should also be a way to filter the workouts from oldest to newest, so that you don’t have to scroll for an eternity if, for example, you’d like to follow the workouts in sequence.
- I have tried to login to my fitness+ account from my Apple TV, but am blocked from doing so because I don’t have an Apple Watch. So i can only access my fitness+ account from my iPhone. This is counterintuitive.
- I have also tried starting the workout on my iPhone and then “sending” it to my Apple TV, which worked initially, but after several minutes of working out the connection was lost and I had to start the workout over from the beginning. Very frustrating.

title: Love it but…
body:
I find the classes to be motivating and I enjoy the variety. 

The videos/workouts completed should be marked as watched. It is difficult to tell what workouts I’ve already done. I also wish these videos went into a watched filter. 

I really like the rowing, yoga and core classes. Looking forward to more options especially in terms of timeframe — a 15min option would be great. 

Another key function I think the app is missing is SCHEDULING. I would like to be able to favorite a timeframe and workout type that automatically adds classes to a schedule so I don’t need to manually select. For example, I like to row 30min on Monday and Friday — if I set this as a preference, the app should populate this for me with new or unwatched videos. A schedule, with alerts, would be yet another factor in personal accountability to commit to a workout plan.

title: Request enhancements
body:
Could you please add a feature to adjust the playback speed of the dance videos? I like the routines, but they‘re just a little bit too fast for me. If I could reduce the speed by 10 to 20%, it would be a great improvement. I‘ve randomly found a few videos that allow you to reduce the playback speed by 50%, but that is way too much.
Another enhancement would be to add some workouts (strength, yoga) that are tailored for people with knee problems. There are a LOT of us out here who either already have or are in the process of ruining our knees. So, workouts without squats or lunges would be great. 
I know the workouts for older adults at least show modifications, but there are only a few videos, and they are, in some aspects, not demanding enough. So, maybe you could create a set of workouts for people who are otherwise strong and in shape, but have to be very careful with their knees. 
This is also one of the reasons it would be good to be able to slow down the dance videos. There can be a lot of torque applied to the knees when trying to turn and step quickly, especially if one is not yet familiar with the basic movement or sequence of movements. I am an ex-dancer, and if I am having problems doing this stuff safely, I’m pretty sure it’s a general problem.

author: Dupuydeg

title: Mixed feelings on this App/service
body:
I just got the Apple SE8 watch. With it was a trial to Fitness+. 

My primary activity is Meditation, so that’s what I’m speaking to largely at the moment. I have to say that so far it feels like this is not a genuine effort for mindfulness/mental health practices. 

My 3 major complaints: 

1) Starting every episode with “…in the apple fitness+ studio in LA…”; this isn’t necessary for the purposes of the audience you’re targeting this activity to. We don’t want to hear “Apple” or promo/marketing narrations about anything while doing this. We already purchase your products and attempt your subscription services like Fitness+; there’s no reason for more efforts at promo.  Dive right into the meditation/lesson and go with it to get your listener into a flowing experience. 

2) Too much repetition; I don’t really want to hear the instructor repeating the same scripted piece multiple times throughout the session. I want it to feel like a true genuine natural lesson directly from the instructor, providing different approaches/stories/perspectives to the lesson at hand. 

3) Obnoxious background music transitions. Whoever edits these with the background music must not be in the mindfulness practice arena. There is not rhythmic or seemingly unnoticeable change in the background music. It just fades out randomly and a different track with a completely different tone/vibe/energy fades in, and often it’s right in a period of silence when the instructor isn’t speaking… that’s very distracting. 

Yes this is mindfulness practice; but I feel as though my guided meditation is being vulnerably released into your hands - Take me through a consistent flowing experience with no unnecessary distractions.

title: Older Runner Needs Strength

title: Life changing
body:

Now with the recent meditations love to see Apple caring about mental health along with physical well being. Thank you Apple for this creation.

However, I use it to track my workouts on the treadmills and the indoor runs are always extremely off.  Over .15 difference per mile.  There will be variables on my time fluctuating 2 minutes per mile when I kept the same cadence and didn’t change any speed on the treadmill.  If Im trying to change my music or using a towel to wipe my face it’s as if it thinks I’ve just stopped running then a slow build up to get the pace back when in reality I never stopped running.

.15 variance per mile when I’m running 6-8 is close to a mile extra I have to run to get my watch to the distance that I ran on the treadmill.  And if I try to go faster on the treadmill the gap and variance grows even larger!

Please fix or give advice on how to correct.  I’ve tried treadmills at different gym and at home and they’re all off.

title: inconsistent and incorrect data
body:
This app is a very cool concept, and got me very excited when iOS 16 came out, making it available on the iPhone. I was have so much fun completely my fitness rings. 
Also, I love how it can connect to other apps that use the Health app like Garmin or Centr. However, the data is not importing over property, throwing off your goals consistently. 
The only way to get the data properly into the the Fitness app is to force the data to import into the Fitness app. For example… open this Fitness app -> then open all of your fitness apps that send data -> reopen this fitness just to verify the import worked. But, even after an important the app is also inconsistent with the data. Meaning it will sometimes add to you ring/goal then hours later remove a lot of your progress from the ring. 
Obviously a lot of bugs that need to be fixed.  But these bugs are some pretty major issues the stop the function or goal of this app. Apple we would definitely love an updated version soon. 😃

title: Helpful, but…
body:
I would really like it if notifications didn’t override the animation for closing rings. It’s such a small thing, but it feels like a reward—especially when it’s a special one, like my favorite watery rings—and gives me the extra motivation to get things done. But when I’m missing it more often than not because my watch thinks it’s more important to give me a notification that I’ve closed the rings or met a goal or something, it makes my ADHD brain less likely to put in the effort over time. Shouldn’t it be possible to be able to access that animation afterward, even if something interrupts? It’s just one of those small things that can actually mean a great deal.

(And yes, I know there’s a feature that turns off the grouping of notifications, but for some reason it still does it anyway. Really annoying and demotivating.)

title: The problem with Fitness+ and similar services
body: I’ve tried Fitness+ and Echelon’s Reflect and both services suffer from the same key issue. When you’re working with people new to fitness form is honestly the most important thing as proper form can prevent injuries. I love old workout videos because they introduce an exercise, they take the time to break down the exercise including what good form looks like and common mistakes. This is done in slow motion with plenty of explanation and then they start the workout. Fitness+ is like hey beginners and right away starts a full-on workout and they’re like hey if you can do it pay attention to the people in the background who will be doing modified versions of the exercises. To date, I have yet to finish even the beginner exercises because it’s frustrating bordering on arrogant of you to assume that a beginner is just going to jump in and my favorite part - not even an option to rewind or jump back - if I want to check ok how was his or her form. That is a place where the Reflect and similar training services have a huge leg up - massive screens and in the case of the Reflect the height, size and brightness works out to where you can literally see yourself next to if not on the trainer so I can literally see if I’m squatting low enough - how does my form compare - the essential things that separate a quality workout from a quantity doing it just to feel good about closing my rings. Technique is a huge part of fitness yet no one wants to take the time to teach it properly.

title: Fitness+ is a bust! Not worth the money
body: For years I had Fitbit. I Loved the app, hated the device. So 4 years ago I bought an Apple Watch which I absolutely love. I liked it so much, I just purchased a new one. The problem is this fitness app. It’s looks pretty but it’s hard to navigate. I was definitely more conscious of my steps with the Fitbit app. However this  Fitness app isn’t as user friendly. I just want to know how many steps I’ve taken. They’re hidden way down at the bottom of the page, under my rings. Also on my phone I’d like to see my weekly/monthly data like a chart. Just like the crappy Apple Calendar app all I see is a dot. I just wish it was more functional and streamlined. I have gained weight and my steps have decreased since using this app. So I tried fitness+. It is a nice concept. I love how when I start a workout on my phone or iPad my watch automatically starts the workout. I like how easy it is for me to workout. However its not worth the money. There’s only 18 beginner workouts and you can’t sort the others by intensity level. I would like more beginner workouts. Maybe some intermediate workouts or even the ability to filter the regular workouts by intensity level. All of the workouts are in the same drab studio. I have not found one that’s set outside. They have no color, no POP! to keep you energized. There’s also not a huge variety of styles of workouts. I thought I’d be able to try new things. All in all I’m just disappointed with the whole Apple Fitness and Fitness+ experience. I will not be paying $10 a month after my free trail ends

title: Excellent app
body:

I tap the exercise icon on my watch if I’m going to intentionally exercise. That way it is specifically tracking.
As far as standing, it appears to track certain movement not just standing, but you can also make it harder/easier to reach that goal. So, if you feel it’s giving you too much slack, make it harder.
I love the sharing option and workouts; very motivating! 
My favorite app and I’ve had many fitness apps.

I wish they would fix this. The app has been around for a couple years now, I’m still hopeful it’ll get only get better.
author: Nikoliosis

title: Love it
body:
Absolutely loving getting back in shape with the workouts.  I particularly love the curated lists that have come out, and the choreographed dance workouts (makes me feel less clumsy overall!)

Would love to see a filter in the future where I could just looked for those choreographed workouts, but otherwise it’s an awesome program!
author: cabuglefish

title: More notification options please!
body: The massive amounts of notifications is so annoying that I want to turn them off. But I do like seeing my friends activities to help motivate me. But can’t they just be lumped together or something? The constant notifications tends to make me ignore ALL of my watch notifications out of annoyance.
author: Tish2277

title: Not colorblind friendly
body: Please give users the option to change the color of the rings and numbers.  It can be really difficult for someone who is colorblind to see the numbers with the move ring.
author: Amyvac

title: Like the workout when they actually work
body: I really like the workouts and trainers. I also like that it syncs with your watch and you can see the progress as the workout goes. I also like that they talk during the workouts because that is a distraction for me in a good way. This is the second time I have paid for a subscription. The first time I ended up canceling it because the app was so buggy especially on the TV. I would be partially through a work out and it would just freeze then I would have to restart the whole thing and there’s no option to fast forward so I had to start from the very beginning, you couldn’t pick up where you left off. happened so many times that I just canceled it the TV. I would be partially through a work out and it would just freeze then I would have to restart the whole thing and there’s no option to fast forward so I had to start from the very beginning, you couldn’t pick up where you left off. Ultimately it happened so many times that I just canceled it. Recently I downloaded it again because I really wanted to focus on squeezing in some exercise into my daily routine. But again the app is so buggy especially on the TV. Today I had 15 minutes so I ran downstairs to start a 10 minute exercise. I spent 10 minutes trying to get a workout to start, I tried three different workouts but it would always freeze then tell me it was unavailable, by that time my opportunity to work out was over as I had ran out of time. I also can’t find where my library is on the TV after I have saved exercises to it.

body: I have an IPhone gen 6th S and it won’t let me download it
author: Hatsunemiku number2

body: You have badges for all kinds of made up dates for alphabet groups but don’t bother to show any support for Independence Day?
author: Andypak79

title: Whhyyyy does my challenge get downgraded the second day of the month?
body:
Why does my fitness app give me a great monthly challenge on the first day of the month only to change it on day 2 to something lame, like “meet your stand goal 1 day”?  

I tried calling and no one knew how to fix this problem. Grasping at straws, they suggested maybe changing some permissions for other apps to write to their app. So I did that and waited another month to see if that fixed it. Nope. July 2 and I’m done. Got my award today because I closed my stand ring one day!!
author: Tangsoosue

title: Good overall
body: If at all possible for us moms and dad out there, can you make a workout that’s pushing stroller with kids. It doesn’t track my movement walking unless my watch is moving and you can’t move your arm while you’re pushing a stroller. Otherwise this is a pretty darn good app for Fitness. You could add this feature I would absolutely love it.
author: violingirl0814

title: Enjoy the workouts!
body:
We were looking for a fitness program that we could both us at home and are very happy with Apple Fitness! We bought an Apple TV to make it easier to use and are happy we did. Love the variety of workouts, and I especially now love the workouts designed for pregnancy.

That said, I could only give four stars due to two factors. I wish there was a better way to filter for workouts, including for intensity. Some days I want a less intense workout but always have to click and read descriptions first. I also wish there were longer stretching videos, separate from yoga or the mindful cooldowns. I would like to see workouts that get into deeper stretching for 20-40 minutes.
author: Lysmin21

title: Worked perfectly until today!
body: Worked perfectly until today! Now it stopped counting my workouts towards my exercise goal. It shows the workouts and my heart rate was above a brisk walk, but the exercise minutes were not adding up. I tried all the suggestions to fix: calibrated, updated, unpaired, repaired, turned off/on, airplane mode, checked location, checked motion, etc.
author: paulagail77

title: Where’d stair tracking go?
body:
Don’t know what’s going on but in the past few days my this app and my paired Apple Watch have stopped accurately counting stairs. The other day only half my numerous trips upstairs were counted. Both last night and tonight it showed 0 instead of 2 after I went up two flights from my basement to the bedroom each time. 

It would be nice to be able to add our own workout categories.
author: Nasus35

title: Nice app, needed improvements
body: Would like to see a tracker for ice bath time and sauna/steam room time.
author: SRHowell

title: Needs improvement
body: The app will pause work out while I’m running….very frustrating when I’m trying to increase my speed and distance…this is no joke a deal breaker here….I run for 3miles it counts everything I really start getting into my run my watch stays on wrist but decides I have paused the workout…like how am I supposed to increase my speed and distance if it randomly pauses..I should be able to trust in the app to continue to monitor my active results….that’s what the app is “designed” to do..I’m not sure if it’s an error between the app and the watch or what but it’s very frustrating to have to look down and pray this app hasn’t paused my workout mid work out. Please fix this small error seeing how all I do with this app is track my calories and my runs. Seriously please this app has the potential to be the very best fitness app. Fix it.

title: Love This App But Have Suggestions
body:
I love this app with the diversity in the trainers, music, and workouts.

But it would be even more improved if it had different breakdowns in the styles of yoga (like yin classes, restorative, hatha along with what is already provided) and adding full-hour practices for those of us used to studio classes.

I’d also like to see a section for kettlebell workouts.

Thank you for considering my suggestions.

So I have to pause my run/exercise to pull out my phone and open the music app to replay music. The rest of the app is great.

body: I like the way the app looks and the variety of trainers. I was looking forward to the walking workouts, but you can't use them without Apple Music. Deeply disappointed I paid for the fitness app and can only use part of it on my phone.

title: Fitness+ workout music option
body:
Really wish there was an option to turn off the music in Fitness+ workouts and just have the trainer’s voice to follow. Then listen to my own tunes or none at all. 
Love the variety of workout types and lengths available. Wish there were 15 minute ones though. There’s a great variety if trainers, which is awesome. 
As far as activity tracking goes, my steps seem short on count compared to when I had a fitbit for multiple years. I averaged quite a few more steps daily back then without changing my lifestyle except my watch.

title: Yoga
body: Hi, I really like the teachers and variety of times and how this works with my watch but would like more variety of yoga styles. Thanks!

The only reason it’s getting 4 stars is because I’ve had my watch and this app since 2018 and I’m only just now hitting the 365 days of working out goal. Kinda discouraging to see but besides that it’s a good app.

title: Freezing problem
body: I love this app and I use it everyday. but the last 2 weeks it has been freezing up on me and I don’t like that. I set goals for my self everyday and I can’t meet them if it freezes up. I’m getting very upset with this what can I do.
author: soulkeeper 😂

title: Swimming Workout Issue
body:
Generally, I think this app is great. Lots of features, works well with Apple Watch and nice integration into both Apple Fitness+ and your own workouts. 

However, there is a terrible problem with looking at previous swim workouts. Instead of displaying the workout in the units it was set to at the time (yards or meters), it displays the information in whatever units was used last!

3x a week I swim long course meters and 2x a week I swim short course yards. If I want to view a workout that was done in different a different unit than my last workout, the information doesn’t display correctly making it useless. 

Couldn’t figure out how to submit a bug report so just leaving a review instead and hope they fix it.
author: SkyInJapan

title: Iphone 13 mini renders this app almost useless
body: I recently purchased an Apple Watch and was excited to try out some workouts with my Fitness+ account, until I realized there is no way to screen mirror the workout video to a larger screen unless you have Apple TV. I can use AirPlay and screen mirror to get other content from my phone to a larger screen, but the fitness workout videos go straight to black when they start. The iPhone 13 mini is a great phone, but not a big enough screen to use workout videos effectively. I will be cancelling my subscription.

There could also be a better way to search for specific exercises. But this app has helped me along with my watch to get myself moving and exercising again. I already have a very hard job that keeps me physical but I definitely needed more exercise.

title: Morning stretches?
body: Was thinking it’d be great to have a series of stretching exercises just to limber up before heading out. They all have stretches at the start but mainly focused on the areas used during the workouts and it seems strange to start a workout just to stretch.  Mindful Cooldown is mainly stretches also but often has meditation or an overall evening feel.

title: Dumbfounded
body: App promises to give you a comprehensive review… of all the stats you’ve been collecting on your Apple Watch … but it simply doesn’t. No stats are available ANYWHERE on the app. There are a selection of fitness opportunities… Video classes… But you will never know how many steps you walked, minutes you stood etc. unless you look at the tiny screen on your watch or your phone. I’m extremely disappointed that there is a description on this app of all the things you wanted the app to do, and yet the app does not deliver them in any way. My next watch will obviously be a Fitbit so that I can see my statistics.

I like that it’ll remind you to end exercises but I wish it could detect your working out and back log your movement into a exercise you pick. Other than that not bad needs better sleep data like for real it’s sad how simple and uninvolved it is compared to whoop and other fitness trackers

author: laurelizabth

title: Not accurate on stairs and miles
body: I have days where this says I climbed 7 or 8 flights of stairs when I maybe went up and down our basement steps a couple times.  Then there’s been days that I went up and down a few times and it doesn’t show any stairs at all.  I think the steps were fairly accurate until I took up crocheting.  Not when I crochet it counts as steps.   Is there a setting that I could set so while crocheting,it doesn’t have me as walking?    Keeping track of my steps was one of the reasons I wanted an Apple Watch that and the alert, if I fall down.   I was in bad shape for almost 4 years and couldn’t hardly get out of bed    Now I’m able to get up and move some, I try to reach certain goals.   Now I have no way of knowing when I really did reach the goals.  I stopped using the sleep part awhile back because it wasn’t accurate either.
author: m. gambs

title: Lack of structure
body: While the array of workouts is impressive, the lack of structure is disappointing. I’ve used other apps that generate new routines everyday based on my fitness goals. Having to wade through all the different workouts is overwhelming to people who are new to working out. I’m 6 months into the Muscle Booster app and I’m happy with my results, but I wanted to try out Apple Fitness. I’m afraid without the structure, I’ll fall off my routine.

body: Started seeing multiple fraudulent recurrent charges from “Apple.com” on my credit card two days after activating my 3-month free trial
author: Jake55555555

body: Wear my watch everyday and use the app to track my sleep and workouts specifically. I would really love a more user-friendly layout where I’m not continually navigating through tabs. I feel like I’m always moving forward through heath data and would really love a more grounding Home Screen with a quick daily recap. I would also love to be able to manually track workouts. Sometimes my watch battery will die or be too low to track workouts by the time I make it to the gym. Being able to go into the app and manually log an hour of spin class, for example, would be really helpful and give me a more accurate look at my exercise routine.

title: Frustrating
body: This app is worthless. Yesterday I worked in my yard for almost 6 hours which included more than an hour mowing my lawn with my push mower. Your app said I only exercised for 28 minutes. Another example is when I do my aqua workout which is at least an hour and a half. It barely registers any exercise, maybe 5 minutes if I’m lucky. Same is true when I lift weights. When I dance it’s slightly better. I dance for at least an hour again your shows 15 minutes of exercise. This dance is intense and makes me sweat like the other forms of exercise.  Very dissatisfied!
author: Bachata*

title: A GREAT at home workout!!
body: I was floundering with how to work out at home after leaving an expensive program, and tried this on the free trial.  I’ve only done two workouts and I loved them both so much I had to review now!  The trainers were awesome with perfect cueing, the music was on point, and I worked up a SWEAT!  I love the diversity in trainers, the joyful smiles and excitement, and my day is going to be so much happier after starting it out with them!  As this app continues to develop, I would love to see intensity ratings on workouts, and more organized programs to follow and reach goals.  Even some guided running intervals!!    BUT, I’m already a big fan, and will gladly use this everyday.  Thank you so much for creating this app to make the best use of all my apple gear!

author: duaneo13

title: I like the app but would enjoy improved features
body: I use the fitness + app often for my workouts. I do love the variety of trainers, workouts, and music styles. I love the diversity of the team as well. I would like it more if there were a feature to allow us to search/filter our saved exercises library. As I save workouts that I’d like to perform I’m finding it difficult to get to specific ones as the list gets longer. It would be great if there was a filter feature so that we could search for what we are looking to do that day. I’d also like it if Apple would allow us to see our rings and exercise progress on our TV when we stream. Currently, it’s only for those with Apple TV and that’s obviously not practical for us without it. Seeing the rings is a big motivator but I don’t want to be reduced to watching my workout on a smaller screen when I’m home just to see rings/progress. I do hope they continue to build their library as well bc I am finding it challenging to get variety with certain trainers as I use it almost daily. It would also be nice if you all had 15 min workout options as well.

title: So disappointing
body:
Fitness+ is great at one thing: making you want to buy an Apple Watch. From there it backslides. First: the tracking is pretty bad. I often get reminders to stand up WHILE I’M STANDING UP. Also, there is no discernible difference between the “Move” tracking and the “Activity” tracking. Admittedly, I don’t sit at a desk all day, so I guess that means I have an active lifestyle, but it must count going up a single flight of stairs as “activity.” Whether or not I close all my rings is a total crapshoot, even if I barely sit down all day. 

But the real disappointment is the Fitness+ subscription workouts. The interface on the iPhone is unusable—so poorly designed. It is so bad it is simply not recognizable as an Apple product. Next, we can’t get it to play on our television, even though we subscribe to Apple+. And when I play it over my iPad, it will not pair with my watch, even though both are running fully updated software and Bluetooth is on.

And lastly, for some bizarre reason, all the instructors are made to constantly wave their hands around when they are introducing their class, which is just comically bizarre. They must feel at least a little self-conscious about it because it is super unnatural looking. I try to laugh it off but you want to be able to take these people seriously. I thought it was just a workout thing but then it happened when I tried a meditation as well (which I immediately stopped and went back to longtime fave meditation app).

 I definitely will not renew when my 3-month free trial period ends. Apple really missed out big time here.

title: Disappointed Daily User
body:
My only substantial complaint about this app is that there are no playback controls beyond play and pause. 

It’s frankly bewildering that users aren’t able to rewind/fast forward through workouts. I understand that the exercise sets are meant to be performed from start to finish in a carefully designed order, but sometimes an Internet connection is spotty, which can cause the video to pause itself to buffer for a moment. It doesn’t take long after that for the app to shut the video down, sending the user to the end-of-workout summary page with a “done” button. At this point, no mater where you are in the workout, the app seems to consider the workout completed with no option to pick up where you left off. After five months of near daily use, this has happened to me several times.

It can happen halfway through a 30-minute workout and with no playback controls, you’re left to wait through the parts you’ve already done or do them all over again if you want to keep your heart rate up while you wait. 

I often squeeze in a workout on my lunch break or in between meetings. So I just don’t have the luxury to stop and wait an extra 20 minutes to return to where I left off. 

I love the trainers. I love the workouts. They’ve taught me an absolute ton about how to move my body properly during exercise, and I feel better and stronger for having these workouts (literally) in my back pocket. 

But the lack of playback controls in the app make create a frequent and significant frustration. And according to the Apple Community Discussions Forum, I’m not alone in my frustrations.

title: Obsessed! Helped me get a 200 Day streak of exercise!
body:
The powerhouse combo of the Apple Watch + Fitness+ has been a game changer for my fitness lifestyle. 

Watch
Love how the watch gives tangible goals for your level that progress with you. Love the dopamine rush when all of my rings close & it makes that little spinning firework. Love that I can congratulate and compete with friends!

App
Love the variety of workouts, especially dance! I’ve always been enamored by dancers but never felt competent enough to join in. These routines meet me where I am, are super fun, & provide a great quick burn. Also love the treadmill workouts! I’ve ALWAYS despised running, especially running “for no reason”… I reluctantly selected a treadmill workout one time at the gym for a quick 10-min warm up, and I’ve been obsessed ever since! It blows my mind that I can actually enjoy something that I’ve been convinced I’ve hated for the last 22 years. 

My only WISH for the app is to have more detailed tracking. Now that I’m getting into running, I’d love it if it would show my previous paces/heart rates for each run I repeat. Same for other workouts (HIIT, cycling, strength, etc. would show heart rate & “lead the pack” placement). Now that this is a lifestyle, it would totally be fun to see if I’m progressing & to have a clear goal to challenge myself again each round.

author: E Vince

title: Leaves you wanting more…
body:
The base app that interacts with you periodically throughout the day is not terrible. It does seem a little inaccurate, but it’s not not bad considering the price point for the watch it’s self. 

The fitness + is definitely lacking. I can see it being useful if you are doing at home workouts with minimal equipment. It even seems to have a good amount of cardio based workouts. However, anyone who was hoping for bench/equipment based workouts is going to be disappointed. 

I was personally hoping to find a list of workouts, or even a list of routines to choose from, for different muscle groups. It would have been nice to build your own routine, choose from existing routines, or even have a personalized one generated. Track your progress, in terms of how much weight you are putting up and reps, and have it more synchronized to your Apple Watch.

 What you get is a list of categories - within those categories are lists of videos that you can click on and follow along with the trainer, and their pupils, in the traditional p90x fashion. Luckily, there is a filter so you could dwindle down the videos to what you’re looking for, but at first glance it’s just a list of videos you sift through to see what you want to try that day. It doesn’t appear to be routines, just different workouts to try, however, new content is added. 

Summary:

The free aspect of the “fitness” app isn’t terrible for what you’re paying for. However, I would wait until they expand fitness +, significantly, before trying this app out - especially if you are looking for bench/equipment based exercises. If you’re looking for high cardio workouts that require nothing but a mat and some dumbbells, this could work for you.

title: Good start!
body:
I love that the workouts start automatically on my Apple Watch, that captions are an option (and some trainers use a little bit of ASL here and there), and that the trainers put out a welcoming and inclusive energy.

What I’d like: 
- More adjustments for people with disabilities (given that they’ve been cleared for exercise by a physician), especially anyone wheelchair-bound. These adjustments can be easy to do, and for some workouts, someone can give adjustment suggestions at the start. Giving workouts that have this option a specific tag would also help.

- Morning yoga, stretch breaks - shorter workouts for when you need to move a bit but don’t have time for a full workout. These could go under the 5min tag in their respective categories or go under a “move break” type category all their own.

- Meditation and stretch cross-overs (under the same 5minute tag I described above). You could even team up with the Ten Percent app for a mini mind-body challenge.

This app has a lot of potential and as time passes, I am getting closer to cancelling my Peloton sub - but it’s not quite ready to replace it yet.
